item.title: A closer look at Verano, AMD's first step toward a Zen-based superchip to rival Nvidia's Vera Rubin
item.description: AMD's upcoming Verano processors aren't like any Epyc CPUs we've seen before. Rather than general-purpose workloads, Verano is designed specifically to power AMD's next generation of GPU servers. In an interview with The Register during a press event in Las Vegas last week, Madhu Rangarajan, CVP of AMD's compute and enterprise AI products business, described Verano as being the first step towards building something that more closely resembles Nvidia's Vera Rubin superchips. "Verano is really designed for an integrated CPU+GPU rack scale solution," he said. "From that perspective, I wouldn't say the CPU is a competitor to Vera. In a head note, I'd say the Verano+GPU solution is a competitor to Vera+Rubin." For reference, Vera Rubin and the GB200 and GB300 that came before it aren't your typical server platforms. Instead they're more like an enormous single-board computer combining CPUs and GPUs into a tightly-integrated package. Each of Nvidia's superchips joins a single 88-core Vera CPU and 1.5 TB of LPDDR5X memory to a pair of Rubin GPUs via Nvidia's speedy NVLink-C2C interconnect. Rangarajan tells us Verano will be the host CPU for a similar class of product using AMD GPUs, and much like Nvidia's superchips, the CPU will also use notebook memory rather than conventional RDIMMS. However, unlike Vera, which is also being deployed as a standalone CPU in storage servers and agent sandboxes, Verano has a singular purpose: keeping its GPUs fed. (We assume they'll be MI500X GPUs.) This design choice reflects AMD's philosophy of one SKU per workload. As such, Verano's core count, clock speeds, memory bandwidth, power, and I/O have been rebalanced to keep its GPUs fed and not much else. Under the hood If we were to peel back Verano's heat spreader, the chip looks a lot like the Venice Epycs we looked at back in September. It features either six of AMD's core complex dies (CCDs) for a total of 72 high-frequency cores clocking to 5.3 GHz, or 192 density-optimized cores clocking to 4.1 GHz, depending on whether the customer's workloads prefer core density or faster clocks. But that's about where the visual similarities end. Much of the chip has been reworked to eliminate data flow bottlenecks between the CPU and the GPUs it is responsible for feeding. The chip features an entirely custom pair of I/O dies through which four LPDDR5X memory controllers are attached. Those memory controllers are currently being validated for use with 24 channels of memory at up to 8,533 MT/s. We're told that we may see that creep up a bit depending on how much headroom AMD has when the part starts shipping next year, but for now that's what AMD is validating against. That means the platform not only has fewer cores, but also slower memory. Peak theoretical memory bandwidth tops out at around 800 GB/s, which you might have noticed is half of what AMD's top-specced Venice parts can do and about 66 percent of Nvidia's Vera. What LPDDR seems to buy AMD is a 30 to 40 percent reduct

item.title: Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent Binance warned iPhone users Tuesday that a publicly released iOS flaw could let malicious apps read files stored by other apps, including the seed phrases and private keys that control crypto wallets. “A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” the exchange wrote on X. “This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.” Binance told users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed IPA files, and to update iOS and every app to the latest official versions. Anyone who suspects a breach should move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions, the exchange said. Neither Binance nor the researcher behind the flaw has reported any thefts tied to it. What worse_query does The bug is a sandbox escape. On iOS, each app is supposed to live in its own container that other apps cannot read. A researcher who posts as forcequitOS released worse_query on GitHub on Nov. 8, calling it “a zero-day sandbox escape for iOS 26 and 27, again.” It succeeds an earlier exploit, bad_query. The project’s README says it works on iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and on iOS 27.2, a wider range than the versions Binance named. It lists paths it can reach, including other apps’ data containers and shared app group folders. The researcher describes it as “a proof-of-concept for developers” that “isn’t useful by itself,” and stresses it is not a jailbreak. To use it, a developer has to build it into an app. That has already happened in at least one case. A day after the release, developer Christoph Kolbicz published a file manager built on worse_query that lets users browse and edit app data on iOS 27 without jailbreaking, which he said was tested on iOS 27.0.1. Blockchain security firm SlowMist called worse_query a container sandbox escape rather than a jailbreak. Its chief information security officer, who posts as 23pds, wrote that the flaw will not steal assets on its own. The risk comes when a user installs and runs an untrusted IPA that then reads other apps’ containers, and only if a wallet stores mnemonic phrases, keystores or WebView caches in plain text on the device. Apple’s iOS updates don’t mention it Apple shipped iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 on Nov. 9, a day after the proof of concept went public. Their security notes list fixes for AirPlay, Bluetooth pairing, brotli and other components, but neither names worse_query or describes a sandbox escape of this kind. That leaves it unclear whether the latest iOS builds block the technique. The exposure depends heavily on how each wallet app stores secrets. item.title: Charvarius Ward Makes Hilarious Comment Explaining Why Lions Won’t Trade for Him
item.description: The Detroit Lions have been connected to Indianapolis Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, but the veteran defensive back doesn’t seem too concerned about being dealt. In fact, Ward offered a pretty hilarious explanation for why he thinks the Lions, or any other team, might hesitate to acquire him. According to Colts beat reporter James Boyd , Ward was asked on Monday about the possibility of being traded. The former Pro Bowl cornerback acknowledged that teams could be interested in acquiring his services before pointing out one rather expensive obstacle. “If you’re a good player and you feel like you got a little value … teams might be interested in you. If a team needs a corner, I don’t know if they’re gonna look for Mooney. Mooney making $20 million a year.” At least Ward is self-aware! Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Indianapolis Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward (7) tackles Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) during the first half at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Have Reportedly Called About Charvarius Ward Ward’s comments are particularly interesting considering A to Z Sports reported that the Lions have already contacted Indianapolis about the veteran cornerback. There is no indication Detroit has made an offer, but general manager Brad Holmes is clearly exploring his options. The Lions have already acquired veteran safety Andre Cisco , and adding a proven outside cornerback could further strengthen their defense. However, with Detroit already facing some important roster decisions in the secondary , Ward’s contract is certainly something Holmes would need to consider. According to the Indianapolis Star , Ward is under contract through 2027 and carries a cap hit of approximately $19.9 million this season with Indianapolis. Ward also indicated that he’s happy with the Colts and hopes to remain there. Whether the Lions ultimately make a move for Ward remains to be seen. But you have to appreciate a player who can laugh about making $20 million a year while explaining why nobody might want to trade for him. Mooney has a pretty good problem to have.

item.title: Rory McIlroy gets brutally honest on Bryson DeChambeau’s outlook after LIV Golf’s shutdown
item.description: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy gets brutally honest on Bryson DeChambeau’s outlook after LIV Golf’s shutdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It was recently announced that LIV Golf is planning to wind down after five years. Bryson DeChambeau was one of the most well known golfers who joined LIV. So, what’s next for DeChambeau ? PGA Tour star Rory McIlroy recently shared his thoughts on DeChambeau’s outlook, via Brentley Romine of Golf Channel. “I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments,” McIlroy said of DeChambeau possibly joining the DP World Tour. “And honestly, look, I’m certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He could attempt to re-join the PGA Tour by first playing in the DP World Tour. Some analysts have questioned if DeChambeau would even consider that path , however. He features a booming social media presence. The idea of DeChambeau sticking with YouTube golf content while making appearances at major tournaments for as long as he’s eligible isn’t out of the question. Of course, DeChambeau would face a challenging path back to the PGA Tour if he were to decide to go in that route, as he was among the LIV Golfers who previously sued the PGA Tour. It remains to be seen how the PGA Tour would handle a potential DeChambeau return attempt. One could argue that neither side needs each other. But is the sport better when they join forces? DeChambeau has become one of the most popular golfers among the younger generation with his massive drives and engaging social media presence. Even McIlroy admitted that DeChambeau “brings eyeballs” to tournaments. The PGA Tour isn’t in a bad spot from a popularity standpoint, but having DeChambeau consistently participate in tournaments surely wouldn’t hurt ratings. Only time will tell what the future holds for Bryson DeChambeau following LIV Golf’s shutdown. item.title: Jontay Porter confesses $500 million revelation, suicidal thoughts after NBA gambling ban in tell-all profile
item.description: Rick Osentoski-USA TODAY Sports. Jontay Porter confesses $500 million revelation, suicidal thoughts after NBA gambling ban in tell-all profile appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After being hit with a ban by the NBA for gambling , former player Jontay Porter revealed how much he bet and some dark thoughts he had after it. Speaking to The New Yorker, Porter revealed that he had suicidal thoughts. He allegedly went to a gun range “just to blow off steam.” One night, he held a gun to his head, which his wife wasn’t even aware of. “I went to the gun range for a few times just to blow off steam, and there was one incident where I—I don’t even think my wife knows this, but, like, held it to my head,” Porter recalled. “I was just, like, crying, like, ‘I can’t do this anymore, I can’t.’ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He was scared that his wife was going to leave him in the wake of everything happening. Porter estimated that he bet around $500 million in lifetime wagers. There was an 18-month stretch where he bet over $50 million at FanDuel. He even took out a $500,000 loan on his house, blowing all of it betting on Russian ping-pong and resulting in him selling the house. Now, Porter is going to therapy for his gambling problem, as he told The New Yorker. Hopefully, he is getting the treatment he needs. The NBA gave Porter a lifetime ban for sports gambling in April 2024. At the time, he was on the Toronto Raptors, his second NBA team. Since receiving the ban, he has continued playing. Porter joined the United States Basketball League’s Seattle Super Hawks in 2026. He led the team to a championship and won league MVP. He previously went undrafted in the 2019 NBA Draft after playing college basketball at Missouri. Porter, the younger brother of Michael Porter Jr., joined the Memphis Grizzlies in 2020. He played in 37 games and started five of them in the NBA. Porter averaged 3.7 points per game. item.title: Mavericks' Kyrie Irving gets major trade update as future with Dallas remains in question
item.description: Mavericks' Kyrie Irving gets major trade update as future with Dallas remains in question originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks have some interesting decisions to make as the trade deadline approaches. Ever since the offseason, there have been a few names that could potentially be on the move. Dallas is 7-4 in a crowded Western Conference, where winning games on a nightly basis will be a challenge. Kyrie Irving has been vocal about focusing on what is in front of the team and continuing to build alongside Cooper Flagg. “We are still growing," Irving said. "We still have a level we want to get to — a higher level. We are going to continue to push each other. We obviously know the external chatter as well and the 15-year age gap and what we are going to accomplish and how we are going to mesh. I think we threw all that out the window and just really focused on what we can control, which is our effort and how we treat each other." Irving's future in Dallas remains uncertain. One thing is for certain: he could be one of the biggest names available on the trade market. “I think he’s going to be the most in-demand player at the trade deadline because he’s not on the Mavericks’ timeline. And we talked about Houston. I think Detroit’s another team that will be salivating over getting Kyrie Irving,” Sports Illustrated’s Chris Mannix said. However, ESPN's Brian Windhorst believes that the injuries piling up across the Western Conference could change Dallas' plans and give the Mavericks a reason to hold onto Irving for a potential playoff run. “Dallas is a team that you know, again, at the start of the season you’re like, when/ if they’re trading Kyrie? Now, you look at what’s happened to the West, Minnesota injuries, Oklahoma City injuries, you’re like, uh I don’t know,” Windhorst said. Keeping Irving in Dallas as a mentor for the younger players wouldn't be the worst outcome, especially considering the value he brings both on and off the court. The Mavericks would like to keep him around for as long as possible. However, another team could make an offer that Dallas simply cannot turn down. Only time will tell. The Mavericks will likely continue evaluating the situation throughout the first half of the season before making a final decision. item.title: HURIWA urges Otti to pay 4,700 teachers
item.description: …Raises concerns over unpaid allowances, rural teachers’ welfare By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has called on Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, to pay 4,700 newly recruited primary school teachers allegedly working without salaries. The association described the reported delay as unfair to the teachers, who it said were recruited and deployed to public schools, particularly in rural communities, but had yet to receive their first salaries since resuming duties last month. In a statement on Tuesday, HURIWA’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, criticised reports that the teachers might not be paid until January 2027 because of a three-month probationary period. “Governor Otti must explain why 4,700 teachers employed by his government should work for months without salaries. These are not volunteering or charity workers. They are employees who deserve to be paid for their services. Probation must not become a licence for exploitation,” the group said. HURIWA also alleged that the teachers’ training allowances had remained unpaid since September, questioning how they were expected to cover transportation costs and meet their family responsibilities without income. The association further asked the state government to explain why the newly recruited teachers were allegedly excluded from the N1 billion reportedly released for teachers during the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration. It said the affected teachers claimed that existing teachers received N50,000 each from the fund, while the new recruits were left out. Beyond the alleged non-payment of salaries and allowances, HURIWA raised concerns about the welfare of teachers posted to rural communities, citing inadequate transportation and accommodation, as well as poor school infrastructure. It urged the state government to deploy some of the electric buses reportedly procured by the administration to transport teachers to rural schools, provide affordable accommodation and teachers’ quarters, and rehabilitate dilapidated classrooms. “Governor Otti cannot claim to be transforming Abia’s education sector while the teachers recruited to drive that transformation allegedly beg for transportation money and wait for months to receive their salaries,” the association said. HURIWA demanded the immediate payment of outstanding salaries and allowances, an investigation into the alleged exclusion of the new recruits from the Teachers’ Day payment, and improved welfare and working conditions. “These 4,700 teachers are not volunteers. They are not charity workers. They are employees recruited by the Abia State Government and deployed to serve the state. Governor Otti must pay them, protect their dignity and provide the conditions they need to teach. Government cannot demand their labour and deny them their wages,” it said. item.title: Seattle Seahawks 2026 trade deadline tracker
item.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. The New York Jets’ Will McDonald IV has reportedly requested a trade and could be one to watch. When does the NFL trade deadline window close? At 4 pm ET/1 pm PT on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The New York Jets have dealt safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-rounder. item.title: Liverpool injury latest: Virgil van Dijk, Dominik Szoboszlai and more
item.description: Liverpool injury latest: Virgil van Dijk, Dominik Szoboszlai and more Liverpool Injury News: Virgil van Dijk, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch Under Fresh Scrutiny Liverpool go into the international break with three points in the bag and a familiar problem hanging over them, availability. The 3-1 win over Crystal Palace steadied things after defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, but that does not change the bigger issue. Andoni Iraola has bodies missing, bodies half-fit and bodies being sent around Europe for international duty when the fixture list is about to turn ugly again. Next up is Manchester United at Anfield on November 22, a match Liverpool should be targeting with absolute clarity. United being down in the relegation zone changes nothing for Liverpool. If key players are absent, the game becomes harder. That is obvious. Iraola knows it, and his public line has been simple enough, get through the break without any more damage. He said: “Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half. Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games. “In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I’m praying, it’s the last thing we need.” Virgil van Dijk fitness concern grows Start with Virgil van Dijk, because when the captain pulls out of the Netherlands squad, people notice. He had been selected by new Dutch head coach Xavi for games against Greece and Germany, then withdrew on fitness grounds. The official explanation was straightforward enough: “Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey have been dropped from the Dutch national team’s upcoming international matches. Both players did not return fit from the past weekend’s matches and are therefore unavailable. “The squad thus currently consists of 23 players.” Photo: IMAGO Liverpool will hope this is caution rather than crisis. Van Dijk has carried heavy minutes before and usually gets on with it. Still, a withdrawal is a withdrawal. You do not pull your captain from international duty for no reason, especially with Nations League fixtures on the schedule. Right now, the sensible assumption is that Liverpool are managing a problem rather than dealing with a major setback. Potential return date: Manchester United (H), Sunday November 22. Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch leave Liverpool short in midfield This is where it starts to bite. Dominik Szoboszlai came off against Crystal Palace with a knee complaint and was clearly struggling before that. Iraola admitted as much. Hungary will assess him after he joined up, which is hardly ideal from a Liverpool point of view. It means uncertainty continues for a player who remains central to the team’s midfield balance, intensity and forward running. Then there is Ryan Gravenberch, absent for Liverpool’s last two matches with a heel issue. There had been some expectation he might make the squad at Selhurst Park, but that never happened. item.title: Bournemouth star receives first England call-up
item.description: Bournemouth star receives first England call-up James Hill Earns First England Call-Up as England Need Defensive Cover England have made a simple, sensible decision. James Hill is in, Ezri Konsa is out for Thursday, and Thomas Tuchel needs cover at centre-back before the Nations League meeting with Croatia at Wembley. Hill, 24, receives his first senior England call-up after a season built on availability and consistency. That matters. He has played every minute of Bournemouth’s Premier League campaign and has also featured in every match of their first Europa League run. Managers notice that. So do international coaches. England Turn to James Hill Konsa’s issue is a knee injury, suffered in the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. He was taken off in that match, although the timeline around his fitness has not been straightforward given he then completed 90 minutes in the win over Hull on Saturday. The expectation is that he will return to full training this week, ahead of England’s game against Spain in Madrid on Sunday. Photo IMAGO For now, though, he is unavailable for Croatia, and Hill gets his chance. Bournemouth Form Drives Selection This call-up has not come from nowhere. Hill joined Bournemouth from Fleetwood in January 2022 for an undisclosed fee, and for a long period he was a squad player, making only 24 appearances across his first three and a half years at the club. That has changed. Last season he became a regular as Bournemouth recorded their highest top-flight finish of sixth. This season he has gone further, staying ever-present while Bournemouth put together an eight-match winning run in all competitions and sit seventh in the Premier League. Defensive Depth Tested Before Croatia England’s defensive reshuffle had already started before Hill’s inclusion. On Sunday, Dan Burn replaced Marc Guehi after the Man City defender withdrew with a hip injury. Tuchel now has another option, and Hill has earned it the hard way, by playing, by staying fit, and by doing his job every week. There is no romance in that, only logic. England needed cover, and James Hill has given them a reason to trust him.

item.title: NFL rumors: Will Giants put Jonathan Taylor trade offer to Colts back on table?
item.description: Travis Register-Imagn Images NFL rumors: Will Giants put Jonathan Taylor trade offer to Colts back on table? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Giants face many questions at the trade deadline. But do they pull the trigger on a big deal? Will they put the Jonathan Taylor trade offer to the Colts back on the table? They may, but what will the offer be? Good Morning Football weighed in, according to a post on X by Ian Rapoport. “The Indianapolis Colts have wanted to be blown away with an offer for Jonathan Taylor,” Rapoport said. “As of right now, they do not have that. How this ends is going to be interesting. Deadlines generally bring about everyone’s best offer.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mike Garafolo added: “I know there was some discussion … about the Giants taking their offer off the table. They could easily just put it back on it. But the question is: Are they willing to go there? And I’m not sure that they’re willing to go back to where they were: the second round and fifth round that they offered to Indianapolis. The Colts may have missed their window.” What would RB Jonathan Taylor mean for the Giants? Head coach John Harbaugh didn’t fully commit to whether the Giants still have interest in Taylor, according to ESPN. “I’m not saying that report’s not true. Those conversations are taking place,” he said following the team’s 19-11 victory over the Eagles. “If something happens for any player, can’t talk about any [specific] player because they’re with other teams right now, but we’re not ruling anything out. “I don’t see anything particularly imminent right now either. So we’ll see what happens. I will say this: Things do change. Things change from day to day.” However, Harbaugh said the team must protect its long-term future. “I’m not just going to go for a short-term fix at exorbitant cost,” Harbaugh said. “That’s not where we’re at. And usually when you do that sort of thing, it doesn’t work out for you. You end paying a hefty price and don’t get the return on it. I never think that you’re one step away or one player away. To me, it’s always just a total momentum kind of thing anyway.” Related: Danhausen tries to ‘uncurse’ Giants after winning Knicks a championship Related: Tiki Barber takes aim at Greg Olsen, FOX broadcast over Malik Nabers fiasco

item.title: NFL rumors: Mike Garafolo warns Jaguars-Eagles Jordan Davis blockbuster could ruin trade deadline
item.description: Credit: Eric Hartline-USA TODAY Sports NFL rumors: Mike Garafolo warns Jaguars-Eagles Jordan Davis blockbuster could ruin trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars have been busy ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline. They have acquired Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles , Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons, and Davon Goschaux from the New Orleans Saints. The deal for Davis was a blockbuster, as the Jaguars sent a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, along with a second-round pick in the 2029 NFL Draft, for the defensive tackle. It was a massive haul that the Jaguars sent the Eagles, and it has been seen by some as an overpay for the defensive tackle. Now, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network is warning that the trade may have major impacts on the trade deadline . “ Jordan Davis . A couple of things. One, this is setting the bar extremely high for the rest of the league right now. And a lot of communication this morning; people are saying, ‘Well, now teams are looking for overpays,’ and that might stall the trade market as we get into the final hours here. That’s number one,” Garafolo said on Good Morning Football. “Number two. Jordan Davis was out of his mind last year, how well he was playing and the fact that he worked so hard to get in shape and have impact plays, as he set himself up for the contract. Got the contract. I’m not saying he slacked off. I’m just saying the production hasn’t been there this season the way it was last year. So many people are focusing on Jalen Carter really not playing as well; Jordan David wasn’t playing as well. So the Eagles are really doing themselves well here by getting this haul.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There have already been plenty of moves heading into the trade deadline. item.title: Why One Top-Tier Starter Won’t Solve the White Sox Rotation Next Season
item.description: Oct 5, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Chicago White Sox pitcher Sean Burke (59) pitches against the Cleveland Guardians during the third inning in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaz… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Lewis Masella, Site Editor With the dust having settled on the Chicago White Sox’s 2026 season, the structural cracks in the team’s engine room have been the focus this offseason. The South Siders still haven’t acquired a top-of-the-rotation ace, which fans expected after general manager Chris Getz said it is part of the organization’s goals in the coming weeks. But acquiring just one top starter while seeking conventional ways to transition relievers to starters is a strategy that will likely fail in the late stages of the 2027 regular season (if there is one, given the looming December lockout). ‎The White Sox covered 2026 with opener concepts, bullpen days, and piggyback tandems to cover a starting rotation that posted just 674 2/3 innings, one of the lowest totals in Major League Baseball. Sean Burke carried most of the burden with his breakout 11-7 regular-season campaign and an elite 3.34 ERA, providing a genuine anchor for the pitching staff. But when the postseason pressure mounted against the Guardians, lack of top-tier rotation depth on the Chicago roster was heavily exposed. Fixing that would cost the White Sox a lot, and considering Jerry Reinsdorf’s deep-seated aversion to spending big for a starting ace, it only reduces the hopes of the franchise becoming a powerhouse in the American League next season. How Many Aces Must the White Sox Acquire? It is tempting to rely heavily on talented young arms, placing a lot of pressure on them to become leaders in the pitching staff. The White Sox system is currently brimming with elite, high-ceiling arm talent. From Noah Schultz to Hagen Smith and David Sandlin , they all represent prospect potential to become top-tier starters. But in 2027, they could only become dynamic mid-rotation starters, including Grant Taylor . This season, Schultz and Smith operated under a strict inning management profile because of their previous struggles with injuries. Oct 7, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago White Sox pitcher Noah Schultz (22) throws a pitch during the fourth inning against the Cleveland Guardians in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Rate Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images ‎Neither has been fully tested with a huge workload in the 162-game MLB regular season. So, throwing them into the fire next year could lead to physical breakdown and development bottlenecks. Or, let us assume that Burke reproduces his 2026 form on the mound and Davis Martin continues to prove serviceable amid his injury troubles; will that be ideal rotation depth that the team will bank on next season? item.title: Why ESPN’s nearly $1.7 billion CFP deal costs the network less than it seems
item.description: ESPN will remain the sole rights holder of the College Football Playoff when the bracket doubles to 24 teams in 2027, under a five-year deal worth nearly $1.7 billion, sources told ESPN’s Heather Dinich . The CFP made the expansion official Monday, and the new terms run through the 2031-32 season. The field will include the four Power 4 champions, the highest-ranked Group of 6 team and 19 at-large selections. The top eight seeds get byes, the first two rounds are played on campus, and the New Year’s Six bowls keep the quarterfinals and semifinals. The selection committee will keep ranking 25 teams each week and could stretch that list to 30 to show which teams sit on the bubble. The national championship game is set for Jan. 24, 2028, in New Orleans. The College Football Playoff logo is painted in the endzone prior to the Cotton Bowl between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Miami Hurricanes at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas on Dec. 31, 2025. ESPN’s added payment averages $345 million a year on top of the roughly $1.3 billion it already pays annually, sources told ESPN’s Pete Thamel . About $140 million of that comes back to the network each year, because the SEC, Big 12 and ACC championship games it holds the rights to will no longer be played. That puts ESPN’s real increase near $205 million a year. Fox, which televises the Big Ten title game, is expected to recoup about $50 million annually. Spread across the 12 new playoff games, ESPN’s net figure comes to roughly $17 million a game, and the network can sublicense six of those games to approved partners. It already sublicenses part of the 12-team bracket to TNT Sports. Combined, the two networks’ recoveries come to about $190 million, so more than half of the new annual payment covers rights fees the leagues were already collecting for their own title games. The ticket, sponsorship and game-day revenue from those events disappears as well. The CFP and ESPN have agreed on a five-year, nearly $1.7 billion deal that will expand the field to 24 teams in 2027 with ESPN as its continued broadcast partner, sources told ESPN, a seismic move that also eliminates the lucrative Power 4 conference championship games. — Heather Dinich (@CFBHeather) November 9, 2026 What happens to championship weekend? The first weekend of December becomes an open week for playoff teams, with the regular season opening in Week Zero, the week before Labor Day, and wrapping up on Thanksgiving weekend. The Army-Navy Game moves into that open weekend in a standalone window, and the Heisman Trophy ceremony is expected later that night. The current policy for the service academies stays in place. If the Army Black Knights or Navy Midshipmen qualify for the field and then lose the rivalry game, their playoff standing is unaffected. In January, the CFP management committee kept the field at 12 for 2026 after the Big Ten, which wanted 24 teams, and the SEC, which preferred 16, failed to agree on a format. item.title: Kennedy Catholic wins second straight CHSAA girls soccer state title
item.description: Kayden Delamere admitted she still is in pain and can’t run at full speed, and she likely will need an MRI to determine the extent of the damage to her ailing knee. It’s one of the reasons tears streamed down her face last Saturday, during one of the proudest moments she has experienced in soccer. “When we won last year, I was just happy,” the Kennedy Catholic senior said. “This time, I was emotional because it felt like we really earned something.” The Gaels had what coach Gareth Horrocks called a “unicorn season” last fall, having everything fall into place to go undefeated. But this run for them was even more fulfilling because it wasn’t perfect, it wasn’t a certainty, and it required even more. So, as Delamere ate with the team afterwards, celebrating fittingly with Buffalo wings, her swollen knee told the tale of sacrifice and triumph against adversity. Kennedy Catholic rallied for a 2-1 victory over Mount Mercy Academy, winning a second straight CHSAA Class A state championship at St. Joseph's Collegiate Institute in Buffalo. Stella Sullivan scored twice, including the winner with 3:07 remaining. Emelia Delamere dribbled through a crowd inside the 30 then lofted a pass ahead to Sullivan on the right. In a spectacular sequence, the sophomore flicked the ball over a defender and retrieved it, then lined a shot into the upper left corner. “The immediate feeling was relief,” Horrocks said. “It was a culmination of three hard months, and we were finally able to take a breath. Then our thoughts went to how proud we are of the girls, and how awesome this was.” The players rushed to mob goalkeeper Stella Siller, then dashed toward the stands, hopping a fence to hug their parents and fans who made the 400-mile trip to support them. “Coming into this season, the outside expectations were incredibly high based on how we performed last year, but the level of difficulty had increased,” assistant coach Paxton Ballard said. “The roster had changed, we dealt with setbacks, and the cards were stacked against us. But we wanted to prove that last season wasn’t an aberration.” Last season, admittedly, was lightning in a bottle. The Gaels went winless the previous year, struggling with participation and frequently forfeiting. With a new coaching staff and renewed interest, the potential of a talented senior core was unlocked in 2025. But more than half of that team graduated, including Liana Crawford, whose eye-popping 61 goals carried the offense. So, this season had the makings of a rebuild. That is, until Kayden Delamere and Sullivan emerged as offensive superstars, and Katelyn Caglione, Lizzy Sinks, Amy Gomez and Brianna Wiley formed a young defense that dominated. Emelia Delamere was excellent, the sophomore shifting between the midfield and back line. The Gaels were undefeated and hit their stride in October, before Kayden Delamere suffered the injury. item.title: Daniss Jenkins Takes Paul Reed’s Spot in Pistons Lineup
item.description: Daniss Jenkins is in the Detroit Pistons starting lineup, and Paul Reed is not. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff changed his starting five for Monday night’s game against the Washington Wizards, going with John Collins, Duncan Robinson, Jenkins , Cade Cunningham and Ausar Thompson. Jenkins did not start against the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday night, when Reed was in the first unit. Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press covered Monday’s postgame press conference and reported Bickerstaff’s reasoning: “On the starting lineup change, JB said Daniss earned more opportunity and they wanted to get smaller and faster by separating Collins and Reed. Said Collins benefitted from the spacing.” Nov 4, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Daniss Jenkins (24) passes in the second half against the Philadelphia 76ers at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Lineup change proved Bickerstaff right for the Pistons Jenkins scored 31 points against the Lakers on Sunday off the bench. He was rewarded with a start against the Wizards, and he followed it with 22 points on 7-for-16 shooting in Detroit’s 122-111 win. Jenkins also grabbed six rebounds, handed out eight assists and took four steals. What Daniss Jenkins does to the Pistons backcourt The change puts Jenkins on the floor next to Cunningham and Robinson from the opening tip and moves Reed to the bench, where he played 21 minutes and scored four points. Collins, the other half of the pairing Bickerstaff split up, had his best night of the season with 24 points and 10 rebounds on 9-for-13 shooting. Cunningham added 17 points. The Pistons are in Washington on Thursday night for the back half of the home-and-home, so the question is whether the start sticks. With the way he has played over the last two games, Jenkins no doubt has earned another one.

item.title: Dolphins Defense Shines While Malik Willis Struggles With Injury
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins defense finally found its rhythm on Sunday, yet the offense could not keep up. Detroit managed only 19 points and 4.6 yards per play against a unit that had struggled all year. The Lions usually average 29 points per game, but they only were able to score 1 touchdown against this Miami squad. Rookie Chris Johnson even grabbed an interception while the run defense held Jahmyr Gibbs to just 74 yards. Despite the strong defensive showing, the loss to the Lions leaves the team at 1-7. The offense sputtered as quarterback Malik Willis looked slow and hesitant on the field. He had two scrambles for only 7 yards, a stark contrast to his usual dynamic play with his legs. Willis has been dealing with a groin injury for weeks, and his movement clearly suffered during the game. The team faces a tough road ahead as they try to find their identity. Defense Steps Up in a Big Way The defensive unit did everything asked of them against a potent Detroit offense. Jared Goff was limited to 6.8 yards per attempt and did not throw a single touchdown pass. This was the first time all season the pass defense allowed a completion percentage below 70 percent. Safety Dante Trader Jr. explained that the coaches emphasized disguising coverages to confuse the quarterback. The plan worked well enough to hold the league’s high-scoring Lions under their typical output. Trader noted that the team is still figuring out exactly who they are on that side of the ball. He feels the defense is trying to become physical while limiting explosive plays. The coaching staff wants to see if they can stick to that identity against tougher teams. The effort was there, but the result on the scoreboard did not reflect the hard work put in by the players. Willis Struggles as Rebuild Continues Head coach Jeff Hafley admitted that Willis had issues with mobility during the game against Detroit. The protection broke down at times, but Willis also lacked the speed to escape the pocket and run. This marks a shift from his earlier performances where he used his legs to make big plays. The injury report lists him with a groin issue, and his reluctance to run is a major concern for the offense. The team is in the middle of a dramatic rebuild with the youngest roster in the NFL. Veteran linebacker Jordyn Brooks calls the situation “Optimistic and hopeful” despite the poor record. Coach Hafley says there is “a lot that I’m really encouraged by” regarding the young players. Yet the hard truth remains that the team is struggling to produce points consistently. Midseason grades from Yahoo Sports highlight that the Dolphins are 30th in the league for on-target passes. Only Tampa Bay and Indianapolis have worse numbers in that category. The article also reminds fans of the old Bill Parcells saying, “You are what your record says you are.” The Dolphins must fix the passing game to win any more games this season. item.title: Cowboys Should Dump Pickens For Raiders Second-Round Pick
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys sit at a crossroads with George Pickens. CBS Sports’ Jordan Dajani pitched a specific deal that sends the Las Vegas Raiders a second-round pick to Dallas in exchange for the All-Pro receiver. The Las Vegas Raiders deal solves a cap headache while giving Frisco a crucial asset for the future. The Cowboys need to pull the trigger before the deadline passes. Playing under the franchise tag this year, Pickens is owed a massive contract. Dajani noted that doubts persist regarding the Cowboys’ capacity to pay him. Then, the recently added Joey Porter Jr. is due a massive contract as well, according to a report . Will Dallas truly commit to paying Pickens approximately $35 million annually? Securing a second-round pick for a player who might not remain on the roster next year is logical. The Raiders Need a True Number One Among wide receiver groups in the NFL, the Raiders possess one of the weakest. With 474 yards, Tre Tucker leads, followed by Jalen Nailor who has 113 yards. For years to come, Pickens would offer Fernando Mendoza a genuine perimeter threat. Leading all Raiders wide receivers this season, his receiving yards total 533. He is an elite deep threat who could stretch the field and open the running game up. Since Las Vegas will not pay a quarterback, they retain the flexibility to offer an elite pass catcher substantial money. Acquiring a player like Pickens for a second-round pick is certainly not a bad price. Last season, he finished third in the NFL for receiving yards. The primary worry is that he will demand compensation comparable to top wide receivers in the league. As Dajani highlighted, $35 million annually is probably the minimum he will request. Cowboys Must Be Willing to Sell Owner Jerry Jones has argued that the addition of Joey Porter Jr. last month from the Steelers is essentially this year’s trade deadline move. But the team needs more help on defense, and the roster is thin on draft capital. However, the Cowboys have a roster member who could facilitate that deal. Dan Graziano of ESPN stated on Monday that George Pickens, the Cowboys’ wide receiver on the franchise tag who appears excluded from future plans and missed Sunday’s game due to injury, is their primary trade asset. Stephen Jones informed 105.3 The Fan on Monday that trade discussions are “pretty quiet on our front.” Yet the Eagles made a blockbuster deal in sending defensive tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville for a first-round pick. For Pickens, the Cowboys might obtain a second-round pick plus some late-round picks for other players. With only four picks in 2027, any trade executed by the team must be a blockbuster. The Cowboys are in a unique situation with a 4-5 record and eight games remaining. They defeated only two teams with winning records since coach Brian Schottenheimer was hired. item.title: Bob Boone Passes Away
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 06: Bob Boone is introduced during an induction ceremony of former Phillies Ron Reed and Bake McBride into the Phillies Wall of Fame before a game against the Washington Nationals at Citizens Bank Park on August 6, 2022 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Rich Schultz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Phillies catcher Bob Boone has died at the age of 78. In addition to being a crucial member of the 1980 World Series Championship team, Boone’s accomplishments in a Phillies uniform include three All-Star appearances, two Gold Gloves, and induction into the Phillies Wall of Fame. Boone played ten seasons with the Phillies, seven with the Angels, and two with the Royals before later managing for both the Royals and the Reds. He was also a part of the very first three-generation family in baseball history. His father, Ray, played 13 seasons with the Detroit Tigers. His sons, Bret and Aaron, also played in the majors. Bret played for 14 years and Aaron played for 12. Aaron is currently the manager for the Yankees. The Phillies are saddened to learn of the passing of former catcher and Wall of Famer Bob Boone yesterday. He was 78. Bob was an incredible player, teammate and family man. item.title: NFL Reporter Linked To Mike Vrabel In Photo Scandal Lands Gig Out Of Mainstream Media
item.description: Dianna Russini is set to resume her career as an NFL insider this week when she launches a new weekly show and column for BetUS Sportsbook. Her new show, “The Russini Report,” will premiere on Wednesday at noon on BetUS TV, with Pro Football Hall of Fame coach Bill Parcells as one of the guests on the premiere episode. BetUS streams live on the gaming company’s website and X account. Sports: Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini Scandal Takes An Intimate Turn In New Report The program will focus on NFL betting and will preview games, break down the head-to-head opponents and use data-backed statistics. Her column will offer analysis on upcoming games. “I’ve spent 20 years chasing the stories everyone’s talking about. Now I get to tell them my way,” Russini, 43, said in a video announcing the show. “Welcome to The Russini Report. Every week I’ll bring you what I’m hearing around the league, why it matters and what happens next. I’ll have guests. I’m going to have opinions. And I’m going to have a lot of fun.” Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost . Dianna Russini interviews Lions quarterback Jared Goff in a game last season. Stephen Maturen via Getty Images Russini, who was previously an NFL insider for ESPN and The Athletic, resigned from the latter in April after the New York Post published photos of her and New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel hugging and holding hands while together at a resort in Sedona, Ariz. They initially stated that their relationship was platonic but Russini decided to resign after The Athletic began an investigation into the matter when additional photos from March 2020 of the pair appearing to share a kiss at a New York bar were released. Sports: Bill Belichick Gets Cranky With Reporter Over Jordon Hudson Breakup Question The Athletic finished its investigation in September, stating that Russini “should have disclosed to The Athletic the nature of her relationship with Vrabel to allow editors to assess the kinds of stories on which she should have been working.” BetUS is an offshore sportsbook based in Costa Rica and licensed and regulated by the government of Curacao, according the BetUS website. Multiple U.S. states have issued cease-and-desist orders against BetUS because of its lack of a U.S. license and regulations. The NFL has not said whether Russini will be a credentialed member of the media at league events going forward. item.title: Pochettino open to Man United talks as Carrick’s future hangs in balance
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino would be open to discussing the Manchester United head coach’s position if the club approaches him, as Michael Carrick faces growing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford. Sky Sports News reports that no final decision has been made on Carrick, while Pochettino is open to talks and could cost United about £7 million to release from his United States contract. United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday to review the season and discuss their recommendations on Carrick. The club is also assessing possible alternatives. Carrick’s position has come under pressure after United went eight consecutive Premier League matches without a win. The team’s late fightbacks in recent matches have offered some encouragement, but have not eased doubts about its overall form. Pochettino, who previously managed Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, recently extended his contract as US head coach through 2030. United have considered him for the Old Trafford job before, but there have been no substantive talks with potential replacements so far. United are expected to use the international break to assess the season before deciding their next step. Carrick remains in charge for now, with the club’s leadership weighing whether a change of coach would address the team’s struggles. item.title: Seven NBA players had their options declined. Here’s what happens next
item.description: On the latest edition of the HoopsHype show, hosts Cyro Asseo and Sam Yip break down the seven players from the 2024 draft class who had their fourth-year options declined. They discuss why teams pass on options, what the move signals to the rest of the league, where each of the seven stands, what history says about players in the same spot and who has the best shot at a long NBA career. You can watch the full episode or check out snippets of the conversation in the transcribed version below the YouTube video. Seven options, $46.7 million, one deadline Timestamp: 00:00 – 01:11 Cyro Asseo: “Seven players from the 2024 draft class just had their fourth-year options declined. Together, those options were worth about $46.7 million. The deadline was Monday, Nov. 2, and it normally falls on Oct. 31, but that day landed on a weekend, so the NBA moved it to a Monday. For anyone new, first-round rookie scale contracts include team options for the third and fourth seasons. If the team declines, the player doesn’t leave right away. He stays for the rest of this season and becomes an unrestricted free agent in the summer of 2027, barring any trades.” Sam Yip: “So this is not a release. It’s a warning, and it puts a real deadline on proving yourself.” Why teams pass Timestamp: 01:16 – 01:53 CA: “Teams pass on options for a few reasons. The first is money. A few million dollars can mean the difference between keeping a player and fitting in a veteran on the market.” SY: “The second is roster spot. Young teams have a lot of young players, and somebody has to go.” CA: “The third is evaluation. The team looks at the player’s development, his minutes, his role, and concludes that continuing this contract isn’t worth it.” SY: “Here’s why it’s a bad sign, even when it isn’t the end. A declined option tells every other front office that your own team doesn’t see the future they hoped for in you. item.title: Jake Walker returns to Turner Motorsport for full-time 2027 IMSA GTD drive
item.description: Motorsport photo Turner Motorsport is set to celebrate a milestone 30th season of professional racing in 2027, renewing its long-standing exclusivity with BMW and welcoming a familiar face back to its full-time driver lineup. The New Hampshire-based squad will anchor its 2027 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship campaign around the #96 BMW M4 GT3 EVO in the GTD class, anchored by full-season co-drivers Robby Foley and Jake Walker. Walker returns to the Turner fold after serving as the team's IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup driver in 2024 and 2025. During his initial stint, Walker impressed with a second-place podium finish at Indianapolis Motor Speedway in 2024 to aid Turner’s second-place finish in the GTD championship, followed by a team-best fifth-place finish at the Rolex 24 At Daytona in 2025. He also scored nine wins to finish runner-up in the IMSA VP Racing SportsCar Challenge GTDX championship that same year. "I’m really excited to be back with Turner Motorsport and BMW Motorsport for the 2027 season," Walker said, noting the confidence he brings into his full-time return. "I’ve learned a tremendous amount as a driver during my first full-time IMSA season, and I’m excited to bring that experience back to the team. I have a lot of confidence in the people around me, and I’m looking forward to getting to work and seeing what we can accomplish together." #96 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT3 EVO: Robby Foley, Patrick Gallagher, Jake Walker, Jens Klingmann #96 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT3 EVO: Robby Foley, Patrick Gallagher, Jake Walker, Jens Klingmann Team owner Will Turner highlighted Walker’s growth as a key factor in bringing him back alongside Foley for a complete championship run. "I’m happy to have Jake Walker back in our GTD car, but this time as Robby’s full-season co-driver," Turner said. "Jake really impressed me as our endurance driver when he ran with us in 2024 and 2025. He and Robby are going to be championship contenders for sure." For Foley, 2027 marks his 10th season with Turner Motorsport and ninth full-time campaign in GTD. The BMW M Works driver – who acts as both a lead competitor and a mentor for younger talent within the team's driver pipeline – comes off a strong campaign where he clinched his fourth title under the Turner banner by winning the Indianapolis 8 Hour and securing the Pro championship in GT World Challenge America, alongside a second-place finish in IMSA GTD. "I’m really looking forward to the 2027 season. It’s going to be exciting having Jake back in the car after a year away from the team," Foley said. "I think we made some significant improvements to our package in 2026. Ultimately, it was a disappointing ending to a great championship run. I’m looking forward to carrying that momentum into 2027 with the whole team and having another great season." With its primary duo set, Turner Motorsport is actively seeking an experienced, funded Silver-rated driver to round out the endurance seat for the IMSA Michelin E

item.title: ADC faults INEC for condemning ‘rig and die’, ignoring APC chairman’s AK-47 threat
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of applying double standards in tackling electoral violence, questioning its silence over an alleged AK-47 threat by an APC chairman against opposition voters. The party said INEC’s condemnation of the ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections was appropriate, but insisted that the commission must show equal urgency when threats emanate from the ruling party. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC recalled remarks attributed to Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, threatening to use AK-47 rifles against those who refused to vote for President Bola Tinubu. “Why has INEC found its voice to condemn ‘rig and die’ but remained conspicuously silent on the threat by an APC chairman to use AK-47 rifles against opposition voters? Is a slogan more dangerous than a gun?” the party asked. It also challenged INEC to disclose whether it had referred the alleged threat to security agencies. “If INEC is concerned about the language of those warning against electoral rigging, should it not be even more concerned when a political party official threatens voters with AK-47 rifles? Has INEC referred the matter to security agencies? If not, why not?” the ADC queried. The opposition party maintained that it rejected electoral violence regardless of the political affiliation of those making the threats. “However, INEC cannot demand peaceful elections without demonstrating equal concern for those threatened with violence. Its responsibility is not merely to condemn inflammatory language, but to demand an environment that permits every Nigerian to vote freely,” Abdullahi said. The post ADC faults INEC for condemning ‘rig and die’, ignoring APC chairman’s AK-47 threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UFC’s Dana White Paid $1.5 Million for 2 Custom Ram Trucks He Was Supposed to Help Auction Off
item.description: THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY; ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA UFC President and CEO Dana White attended the Barrett-Jackson 2026 Las Vegas auction to help sell two custom Ram trucks for charity, but he ended up buying them himself. “That was my first car auction. That escalated quickly,” White, 57, joked in a post-auction video after paying $1.5 million for the trucks. THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY “Watching Dana White battle other bidders for the pair of custom charity Ram trucks was incredibly special — a moment enthusiasts will never forget,” Craig Jackson , chairman and CEO of the company, which is known as the world’s greatest collector car auctions, said in a press release . The auction took place on September 11, in remembrance of the 25th anniversary of the 2001 terrorist attacks. Because the auction house waived all fees and commissions, 100 percent of the hammer price was shared equally between the Folds of Honor Foundation, which provides educational scholarships to the families of America’s fallen or disabled military and first responders, and the UFC Foundation, which will use the money to help support Hispanic charities. “Dana is one of the most patriotic individuals in our country, and it is fitting that his winning bid on 9/11 will benefit those in need, especially the families of fallen American service members and first responders,” added Jackson. THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY “It’s a great charity, it’s going to help a lot of people and I like that I’m leaving here with these two trucks,” White added of the vehicles, which were designed in collaboration between Ram, UFC, RealTruck and Barrett-Jackson. White’s donation bought him the first retail production and custom one-of-one 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT Pickup and a pristine custom 2005 Ram 1500 SRT-10 Pickup. “Every build tells a story. This one tells three. It’s a 2005 truck, the same year UFC’s Ultimate Fighter launched under Dana White and this SRT-10 became the inspiration for the new Rumble Bee it’s paired with,” RealTruck Inc. Vice President of Marketing Lee Riser said in a press release . “We took RealTruck’s product lineup, Ram’s performance DNA, and UFC’s massive platform, and pointed it all at something bigger: raising real money for Folds of Honor and the UFC Foundation through Barrett-Jackson’s stage,” he added. “This is how you build a legacy piece with a purpose and we’re excited to have this heavyweight added to our collaboration lineup.” Read More From InTouch Weekly ‘16 & Pregnant’ Alum Whitney Purvis Pleads Guilty to Involuntary Manslaughter Case After Overdose Death Kaia Gerber Shares Emotional Quote About Grief Following Brother Presley’s Death at 27 Russell Brand Is a 'Dead Man Walking' in Prison as Ex-Inmate Issues Chilling Warning This story UFC’s Dana White Paid $1.5 Million for 2 Custom Ram Trucks He Was Supposed to Help Auction Off first appeared on InTouch Weekly . Follow InTouch Weekly on Yahoo so you don’t miss what’s coming next.

item.title: Police arrest two over N1.35m robbery in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested two suspected armed robbers over the theft of N1.35 million and other valuables at Falgore Forest in Doguwa Local Government Area of the state. The suspects, identified as Sulaiman Alhaji Umaru, 35, from Kaduna State, and Abubakar Sale, 22, from Gwarzo Local Government Area of Kano State, were arrested on November 6 at Dogon Dutse, Falgore Forest. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday, saying operatives of the Doguwa Division made the arrests following credible intelligence. According to Kiyawa, one of the suspects, Umaru, confessed to conspiring with seven others to rob Adamu Sa’adu of N1.35 million and other valuables in the Falgore Forest area. He said the police recovered N600,000, nine mobile phones, knives and sticks from the suspects. The command said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the remaining suspects, while investigation into the robbery continued. The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the officers for the operation and urged residents to continue providing credible information to support efforts to tackle crime. He assured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state. The post Police arrest two over N1.35m robbery in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Loanee reports: Not in Serie A
item.description: It’s happening. I repeat, it’s happening. | DeFodi Images via Getty Images Maat Daniel Caprini (Cesena) It’s been a rocky start to the season for the 20-year-old winger. He missed the first few months with a hamstring injury and has only just gotten back into the match day squad, making a couple appearances off the bench. He’s looked lively but still a bit off-kilter, missing several presentable chances. If coach Alessandro Diamante can help him put together all his talent, he could be ready for a much bigger role next year. Caprini’s got all the talent in the world but just needs to process the game a little quicker. The first step is reclaiming a starting role. Next is producing in the final third. Loan terms : option with a buyback, no amounts listed anywhere Stats : 3 appearances (1 start) Grade : C+ Needs to get on the pitch and make things happen and I think he can do just that Lapo Deli (Empoli) The 20-year-old midfielder has done well to seize a significant role for the Azzurri. He looks like the 5th-choice central midfielder in Matteo Andreolotti’s 3-5-2; with Empoli sitting in 18th, there’s a decent chance that the mister will shake things up and give him some more minutes. It’s harder to analyze a holding midfielder from short appearances than it is an attacker but I think Deli’s avoiding mistakes rather than taking the initiative. Loan terms : option with a buyback, no amounts listed anywhere Stats : 6 appearances (0 starts), 2 yellow cards Grade : C+ Needs to string together a few starts. Gino Infantino (Argentinos Juniors) The former Argentina U20 captain hasn’t thrived in his home nation. He made a couple appearances off the bench in the Apertura but has yet to feature in the Clausura, which means he hasn’t played since March. He’s spent nearly as much time in the stands as on the bench and I can’t help but wonder if Nicolás Diez has decided he isn’t up to snuff and is ensuring he doesn’t play enough to trigger a purchase. It’s a tough situation for a young guy and made worse by the fact that the club itself made him an object of fun with its announcement video . Loan terms : conditional obligation, no amounts listed anywhere Stats : 2 appearances (0 starts) Grade : F It’s just not happening for him. Tommaso Martinelli (Avellino) Up front, I don’t understand goalkeeper evaluation all that well but from what I’ve seen, the 20-year-old kid from Bagno a Ripoli is progressing well. Despite his ursine build, he’s got superb reflexes but what stands out to me is his anticipation: he’s great at moving his feet early so that he just has to smother the ball instead of diving for it. He also loves a quick throw to start a counterattack. He’s still learning to time his charges off his line but all in all, I’ve enjoyed him. He’s also got a great attitude, it seems like, minimizing the barking he does at his teammates and just getting on with it. item.title: Stephen A. Smith sounds off on Vikings, Justin Jefferson trade speculation
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings are 6-2 after the Buffalo Bills defeated them 23-6 on Monday Night Football. Their defense held up as long as it could, but Bills stars Josh Allen and James Cook eventually broke through. Vikings QB Carson Wentz was pretty horrible, and star receiver Justin Jefferson was visibly frustrated. They still have a good record and a great chance to make the playoffs. Minnesota has a glaring quarterback issue, and head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn’t been able to get the most out of Wentz or Kyler Murray . ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith weighed in on the job O’Connell has done and whether Jefferson should demand a trade. MORE: Vikings have quarterback problem without real solution What did Stephen A. Smith say about Vikings? Sep 27, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Smith isn’t afraid to go after someone and give a hot take. Well, he did that on “First Take” this morning. He had this to say about Jefferson and O’Connell: It’s awful. It’s really, really awful. And I’m going to say this. Listen, Justin Jefferson, fellas, Shea, this man should ask to be traded. If you’re Kevin O’Connell… I’m talking to Kevin O’Connell, the head coach of the Minnesota Vikings. You’re lucky Justin Jefferson even talks to you. Seriously. Because what he has done to this man’s career, I’m holding him responsible. I’m holding ownership responsible” “[Justin Jefferson] should ask to be traded.” @stephenasmith unloads on the Vikings and Kevin O'Connell after their loss to the Bills 👀 pic.twitter.com/PeKqGxhMV9 — First Take (@FirstTake) November 10, 2026 The Vikings are wasting an insanely good defense and a generational wide receiver. Jefferson has 31 receptions for 389 yards and four touchdowns. Who knows what those numbers would be like if he had a somewhat competent quarterback. Smith is right that O’Connell hasn’t done a good enough job developing quarterbacks, and the decision-makers on roster moves have failed Jefferson by not providing somewhat decent quarterback play. What moves could the Vikings make at the trade deadline? Kirk Cousins | David Berding/GettyImages The Vikings have made it clear they’re looking to bring in a veteran quarterback like Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones to make the most of this season. The trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET today! From @GMFB : After a woeful offensive performance on MNF, the #Vikings are expected to explore options at the QB position. pic.twitter.com/sY5o2ZfWpR — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 10, 2026 Reuniting Cousins and O’Connell makes the most sense because of their history together. The duo wouldn’t be starting from scratch, and the Las Vegas Raiders ‘ QB knows how to play with a star wideout like Jefferson. Minnesota won’t be trading Jefferson, but it will be a spicy talking point once this

item.title: Army renames Calabar barracks after late COAS Attahiru
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Army has renamed Akim Barracks, Headquarters 13 Brigade, Calabar, Cross River State, after the late former Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Ibrahim Attahiru, in recognition of his service and sacrifice to the nation. The renaming ceremony was performed on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, by the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, during his operational visit to Cross River State. A statement by Army Headquarters said the honour recognised Attahiru’s exceptional service, exemplary leadership and ultimate sacrifice in defence of the country. Speaking at the ceremony, Shaibu described the renaming as a deliberate act of remembrance and an enduring affirmation of the institutional values that define the Nigerian Army. He said the late general exemplified courage, professional competence, discipline and selfless devotion to duty, particularly during a challenging period in the country’s security history when the Army faced complex and evolving threats. Although his tenure as COAS was brief, Shaibu said Attahiru’s commitment to operational effectiveness, personnel welfare, professionalism and the fighting spirit of troops continued to resonate within the Army. He noted that immortalising the late military chief, who once commanded the barracks, went beyond preserving his memory, as it established a lasting connection between the Army’s heritage and the responsibilities of present and future generations of military personnel. The COAS charged officers and soldiers of 13 Brigade to reflect the honour through exemplary leadership, discipline, integrity, operational excellence and stronger relationships with the communities they were deployed to protect. He further urged them to uphold the highest standards of military conduct and contribute to building a well-trained, adequately equipped and highly motivated force capable of discharging its constitutional responsibilities. Earlier, the General Officer Commanding 82 Division of the Nigerian Army and Commander of Joint Task Force South East, Operation Udoka, Major General Ayobami Fadairo, commended the COAS for his commitment to troop welfare and the decision to immortalise the late general. He said the gesture would strengthen institutional pride and boost the morale of personnel serving in the division. The Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, represented by his deputy, Dr Peter Odey, also paid tribute to the late military chief, describing his life as an enduring example of exemplary leadership, humility and patriotism worthy of emulation, particularly by military personnel. In her remarks, the wife of the late general, Mrs Fatima Attahiru, thanked the COAS and the Nigerian Army for the honour, describing it as a lasting source of pride and comfort to the family. The ceremony was attended by senior military officers, government officials, members of the late general’s family and residents of the bar

item.title: What does SEC Championship Game ending mean for Atlanta’s economy?
item.description: FILE - Georgia head coach Kirby Smart is handed the SEC trophy by Commissioner Greg Sankey as the team celebrates after a Southeastern Conference championship NCAA college football game against Alabama, Dec. 6, 2025, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart, File) Mike Stewart For more than three decades, the SEC Championship has brought thousands of fans to downtown Atlanta each December to fill the stadium and nearby hotels, bars and restaurants. That will change starting in 2027. The SEC announced Monday that this year will be the final SEC Championship Game to align with the College Football Playoff expanding from 12 teams to 24 teams. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Atlanta has hosted all but two of the SEC Championship Games, first at the Georgia Dome and now at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. David Epps, CEO of the Chick-fil-A Peach Bowl, says Atlanta will feel economic impact of losing the championship. “So I would imagine that losing the SEC Championship Game probably has a $45 to $55 million economic impact. So that’s not an insignificant loss for Atlanta, but Atlanta as a city performs best when it’s under stress,” Epps told Channel 2’s Ashlyn Webb . WHY IS ATLANTA LOSING THE SEC CHAMPIONSHIP? One of college football’s traditions is coming to an end because of the playoff expansion. The College Football Playoff and ESPN agreed to a deal to expand to 24 teams and swift the entire calendar. The weekend that has been reserved for conference championships will likely become the first round of the playoff. “And ultimately there was just no room left in the schedule for it,” Epp said. While Atlanta is losing the SEC Championship Game, Epps says the Chick-fil-A Playoff will continue hosting their playoff game. “Things evolve, and I think we’re all going to love college football in the future as much as we love it now,” Epps said. By the time it became clear the Celtics would be moving on from Jaylen Brown this past offseason, most fans thought he would be traded into a situation where the five-time All-Star would be a clear-cut No. 1 option for the first time. The opposite became true. Brown's stunning trade to the 76ers in July, which opened the door for Philadelphia to add LeBron James weeks later, put him on a team loaded with star talent and a ton of experience. There were a lot of questions entering 2026-27 about how Brown would fit alongside James, Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid, and whether he could still make the same kind of impact he did in Boston. With Brown set to face his former Celtics team for the first time on Tuesday night, he's now 10 games into his Philadelphia career — and for the most part, he's been just as valuable to his new team, shutting down concerns over how the 76ers' stars would share the ball. Here's a look at how Brown has played early in his first year with the 76ers. MORE: Celtics Reportedly Ignored One Request From Jaylen Brown Before Trading Him First Impressions of Jaylen Brown With 76ers Concerns over 76ers 'mouths to feed' haven't stopped Brown After the 76ers' huge offseason, trading for Brown and signing James while adding Dean Wade and Anfernee Simons to their bench, the top concern fans, analysts and more had about the team was how it would mesh a collection of All-Stars together — especially when it became apparent in Boston that Brown wanted to be treated as a No. 1 star. Through 10 games, Philadelphia has quieted those concerns, and Brown is a major reason why. With the 76ers sitting at 9-2 entering their first game against the Celtics, they've immediately become one of the NBA's best teams, proving they can beat opponents in a variety of ways. And Brown has consistently found ways to get involved, whether on or off the ball. He dropped a season-high 30 points against the Pistons on Nov. 4 in a 76ers win, but even on nights like Philadelphia's season-opener against the Knicks, he's contributed to winning by making an all-around impact and remaining efficient. In that win over New York, Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists on 7-of-14 shooting. While Tyrese Maxey has emerged as the clear No. 1 scorer for Philadelphia, Brown has been willing to defer when needed, but also take the reins of the offense in spurts. Emotions ran high inside U.S. Bank Stadium in Minnesota on Monday night. During the Minnesota Vikings’ primetime clash against the Buffalo Bills on Monday, Nov. 9, Master Sergeant Kelsey McLeod surprised her two daughters and parents when she was recognized as part of the NFL’s Salute to Service initiative. In an emotional moment shared on ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast, McLeod’s family stood in the endzone wearing Vikings jerseys during a break in play. McLeod then surprised them as they walked off the field. Master Sergeant Kelsey McLeod surprises her family at the Bills-Vikings game on Nov. 9, 2026. Credit: Minnesota Vikings/Instagram The stadium erupted with cheers as McLeod reunited with her loved ones after 473 days apart, as she was on assignment in Korea. McLeod sweetly embraced her mom and dad while tearfully taking in the moment with each of her daughters in her arms. View this post on Instagram “Military family getting a visit and a video from the two girls on the far left’s mom saying, ‘Girls, I’ll be home soon’,” ESPN’s Joe Buck said on Monday’s broadcast as the events unfolded on the field. “Well, little did they know soon was right now.” Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “Kelsey McLeod reunited with her two daughters and her parents after 473 days apart following an overseas assignment in Korea. It’s just a beautiful thing to watch,” Buck added. The Bills went on to defeat the Vikings, 23-6. Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on Nov. 9, 2026.
