item.title: Jets might've missed a huge opportunity amid Jaguars trade interest in Will McDonald Iv
item.description: Jets might've missed a huge opportunity amid Jaguars trade interest in Will McDonald Iv originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets have not made a significant trade before the 2026 NFL trade deadline yet. They sent Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a sixth-round pick, which is a solid deal for a poor 2-7 Jets team. While Breece Hall and Garrett Wilson have popped up in trade rumors, neither is likely to go. The same cannot be said for edge rusher Will McDonald IV. He's been mentioned in trade rumors, but the Jets have made it clear they want to keep the 27-year-old edge. However, that might've been a big mistake, as the report from Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer on McDonald revealed the Jacksonville Jaguars made a "significant" offer for McDonald that the Jets maybe should've taken considering the moves the Jaguars made. Jets might've missed chance to land haul from Jaguars for Will McDonald IV "The trade request of Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV is interesting," Breer writes. "The Jaguars, before the flurry of action on Monday, had made a significant offer for him." Unfortunately for the Jets, that significant trade offer might now be off the table. The reason why? The Jaguars made two massive moves on Monday. They sent a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III, and then the Jaguars sent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis. Those were two massive moves for the Jaguars, and trades that could be seen as overpays. If the Jaguars were willing to spend so much on Bates and Davis, it would stand to reason that they would've offered a lot for McDonald. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade While there's not been any confirmed reporting on what the Jaguars "significant" trade offer for McDonald was, if it was equal to or more than a third-round pick, this might've been a huge missed opportunity for the Jets. McDonald requested a trade, which would indicate his time with the team might be coming to an end. Instead of trading him, the Jets have pushed the narrative that he's a key piece of their defense going forward. However, with a chance to get a significant return from the Jaguars on the table, the Jets didn't take it based on the Jaguars' trades for Davis and Bates, and now such an offer might not be in play. It's too soon to say the Jets made a massive mistake, but there's no denying that this was a missed opportunity to get a likely very strong haul for McDonald after the edge rusher requested a trade. item.title: Lens sack coach after 9-1 defeat to Como in Champions League
item.description: Lens have sacked coach Yannick Cahuzac less than a week after their 9-1 Champions League defeat at home to Como, a source close to the French club told AFP on Tuesday, confirming a report from sports daily L’Equipe. Cahuzac, who was appointed by Lens less than two months ago, lost his job after the French Cup winners’ humiliating loss to Como last Wednesday, as well as a subsequent 2-1 reversal at their Stade Bollaert-Delelis home against Marseille on Sunday in Ligue 1. “We feel like we’re in a bad way. We feel that Wednesday’s result has left its mark,” Cahuzac admitted after the match against Marseille. “We’ve managed to pick ourselves up. But we’ve got quite a few gaps in the team, and we feel we’ve lost our confidence.” The former Lens captain took over from Dino Toppmoeller in mid-September following the German coach’s surprise departure after just four Ligue 1 matchdays. In nine matches in charge of Lens, Cahuzac has secured just three wins and suffered six defeats across all competitions as Lens lounge in 11th place domestically. Crucially, the 41-year-old has failed to pick up a single point in Europe, losing to Sporting Lisbon and Club Brugge, as well as the Como thrashing — the joint record for the biggest winning margin in the modern Champions League. “In front of our fans, here at Bollaert, this is unacceptable,” Lens chairman Joseph Oughourlian told Ligue 1+ on Sunday, adding that he had had the words “never again” painted on the walls of the changing room. Last season under current Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage, Lens won the French Cup and finished second in the league behind Paris Saint-Germain. The post Lens sack coach after 9-1 defeat to Como in Champions League appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Awkunanaw youths endorse Mbah, Tinubu
item.description: …Reject rival governorship bids, pledge support for APC candidates By Chinedu Adonu Youths from Awkunanaw in Enugu State have endorsed Governor Peter Mbah for a second term and President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, pledging to mobilise support for all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the state. The youths, under the aegis of the Awkunanaw Political Forum (APF), also rejected governorship ambitions by other Awkunanaw indigenes seeking to challenge Mbah, urging them to shelve their aspirations and support the incumbent governor. The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued on Tuesday following the group’s youth-led convention held at the Enugu South Local Government Secretariat on November 10, 2026. The communiqué, signed by the Director-General of APF, Hon. Nnamani Arinze Darlington, and the Executive Chairman of Enugu South Local Government, Hon. Caleb Onyema Ani, said the endorsement followed extensive consultations on the political and socio-economic development of the state. Declaring their support for Mbah, the group cited his administration’s investments in education, healthcare, roads, transportation and security. It specifically highlighted the establishment of 268 Smart Green Schools, 260 Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres, construction of over 1,521 kilometres of roads, five transport terminals and the deployment of more than 100 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses. The forum also commended the governor for reviving moribund state-owned assets and completing abandoned projects, including Hotel Presidential, Nigergas Limited, Enugu United Palm Products Limited and the International Conference Centre. Describing Mbah as its preferred candidate, the group said his leadership and development agenda aligned with the collective aspirations of the people of Enugu State. Explaining its opposition to other Awkunanaw governorship bids, the forum recalled the support it said Nkanu East Local Government Area gave former Governor Chimaroke Nnamani during his tenure. “Our brothers from Nkanu East LGA showed us support during His Excellency, Dr Chimaroke Nnamani’s tenure. We can only return the favour by standing in solidarity behind the governor,” the communiqué stated. The youths also endorsed Tinubu for a second term, citing his administration’s economic reforms, Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) student loan scheme, consumer credit initiative, infrastructure projects and Presidential CNG Initiative. “We pledge our unalloyed loyalty to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and commit our organisational strength to ensuring total victory for him in 2027,” the communiqué stated. The forum further pledged to mobilise and campaign for APC candidates seeking legislative and executive positions across Enugu State. It urged Awkunanaw youths to remain united and actively participate in the political process, declaring: “One Voice. One Destiny. Awkunanaw for APC!” The post 2027: Awkunanaw youths endorse Mbah, Tinubu appeared first on Va

item.title: 2027: Jigawa is APC stronghold, Shettima claims
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse Vice President Kashim Shettima has claimed that Jigawa State is firmly behind the All Progressives Congress (APC), alleging that the four former governors of the state, including Sule Lamido, are supporting the ruling party. Shettima made the claim on Tuesday during the APC presidential campaign rally in Dutse, the state capital. He expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would secure massive votes in Jigawa in the 2027 presidential election, describing the state as an APC stronghold. According to him, prominent political figures in the state, including former governors Ali Sa’adu, Ibrahim Saminu Turaki, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar and Sule Lamido, are aligned with the APC. “Jigawa State is a home for the APC. All who and who, any politician who answers a name is with us. The former governors of Jigawa State, Ali Sa’adu, Ibrahim Saminu Turaki, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, and even former Governor Alhaji Sule Lamido, are with us,” he said. Shettima, however, criticised the African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, over his comments accusing the late former President Muhammadu Buhari of deceiving him. The Vice President described Amaechi’s remarks as disrespectful to the North, saying Buhari remained one of the most respected political figures in the region. He said Northerners were known for their generosity and culture of appreciating and reciprocating acts of kindness. Shettima urged Jigawa residents to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections, saying it was time for the North to reciprocate what the President had done for the region and its people. He called on residents to turn out in large numbers to vote for Tinubu and all APC candidates, expressing confidence that the party would record a landslide victory in the state. item.description: …No other Nigerian leader has radically transformed Nigerian than Tinubu-Alake boasts …Nigeria has been recording positive growth since Tinubu became President …Tinubu has given opportunity for 1.6 Nigerians to go to university-Idris By Soni Daniel (Northern Region Editor), Emma Ujah (Bureau Chief, Abuja) & Omeiza Ajayi President Bola Tinubu will pay priority attention to the protection of lives and property if he wins the forthcoming presidential election on January 16, 2027, the All Progressives Presidential Campaign Council revealed on Tuesday in Abuja. To achieve that objective, the party has promised to recruit 28,000 additional military personnel and 50,000 police officers, in order to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. Beyond security, the APC administration under the leadership of President Tinubu plans to provide better quality and more affordable life for Nigerians; energy, infrastructure and economic growth, effective and accountable government. The Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, who is the Deputy Director, Directorate of Manifesto and Policy Development of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, made the declaration with the theme: “Transiting from Reforms to Shared Prosperity”. The party also promised to complete the establishment and equipping of the four new Army Divisions in Makurdi, Ilorin, Jalingo and Benin City; sustain intelligence-led kinetic operations against insurgents and kidnapping networks to degrade and dismantle their operating bases. In order to deal with kidnappers who have turned the nation’s forests into criminal hideouts, the ruling party promised to deploy trained Forest Guards, Agro-Rangers and Mining Marshals to safeguard agricultural belts, farming communities, grazing routes, national forest reserves and mineral deposits. The minister said the APC administration planned to make Nigeria a fortress where everyone would live happily to actualize their potentials without any form of fear. item.title: High oil prices have led to a dip in global carbon emissions
item.description: Evaluating the annual global temperatures each year requires context. There is a fair amount of natural variability from one year to the next, so it’s important to focus on the trend over time. Famously, global warming did not end in 1998, as some claimed a couple of decades ago—we just had a run of La-Niña-dominated years after a very strong El Niño. Annual greenhouse gas emissions are much less variable, having increased fairly steadily, but many complicating factors can still muddy the picture. Sometimes those factors conspire to throw a year off the trend. It looks like 2026 will be one of those years. A new analysis led by Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia estimates that fossil fuel emissions have fallen about 0.4 percent from last year. This probably isn’t a peak that symbolizes heartening progress on climate change, though; the researchers think it’s a short-term dip driven by the war in Iran and its effect on oil prices. item.title: Troops rescue 21 kidnapped victims in Niger
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 18 Brigade of the Nigerian Army have rescued 21 kidnapped victims following a gun battle with terrorists in Mariga Local Government Area of Niger State. The operation was conducted on Monday, November 9, 2026, after troops acted on intelligence about the activities of terrorists in Abaha and Sabon Wuri villages. The Brigade’s spokesman, Captain Adebayo Adewumi, said the troops deployed a fighting patrol to the area to intercept the criminal elements. He said a fierce gun battle ensued when the troops made contact with the terrorists, who were eventually overpowered and forced to flee into the nearby bush with suspected gunshot wounds. According to him, all 21 kidnapped victims were rescued unharmed and handed over to the appropriate authorities for reunification with their families after receiving first aid and undergoing preliminary profiling. Adewumi said troops had intensified operations through aggressive patrols and ambushes to track down and apprehend the fleeing terrorists. He urged residents of Mariga and neighbouring local government areas to promptly report anyone seen with gunshot wounds or any suspicious movement of criminal elements to the nearest security agency. The spokesman said the Commander of the 18 Brigade commended the troops for their gallantry, resilience and professionalism during the operation. He added that the commander had charged them to sustain the offensive and maintain operational momentum to rid the brigade’s area of responsibility of criminal activities and ensure the safety of law-abiding residents. Adewumi also attributed the operational gains to the recent expansion of the Nigerian Army and the additional operational capacity it had provided in the fight against kidnapping and terrorism in Niger State. item.title: UK, Nigeria deepen cooperation against financial crimes
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The United Kingdom and Nigeria have strengthened their strategic partnership to combat illicit financial flows, money laundering, fraud and terrorism financing through enhanced financial intelligence sharing and cross-border cooperation. The renewed cooperation followed high-level engagements in the UK involving Nigerian financial authorities, regulators and stakeholders from the banking and telecommunications sectors, according to a joint statement issued on Tuesday. The Nigerian delegation was led by the Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), Hafsat Bakari, and included representatives of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC). A major highlight of the visit was an engagement with the UK’s Joint Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce (JMLIT), a public-private partnership involving law enforcement agencies, regulators and private-sector institutions. The engagement provided an opportunity for both countries to exchange expertise on financial intelligence, information sharing and strategies for identifying and responding to illicit financial activities. The discussions also supported Nigeria’s plan to establish the Joint Financial Intelligence Cooperation (JFIC), a Nigerian-led initiative aimed at strengthening collaboration between government institutions and private-sector stakeholders. The initiative is expected to enhance the country’s capacity to detect and respond to money laundering, fraud, terrorism financing and other financial crimes through technology-driven cooperation and information sharing. During the visit, the delegation also met with representatives of the National Crime Agency (NCA), UK Financial Intelligence Unit (UKFIU), HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC), Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and HM Treasury. The discussions covered operational cooperation, trade-based money laundering, emerging financial threats, the UK’s Financial Action Task Force (FATF) presidency and opportunities for stronger international collaboration. Speaking on the partnership, Deputy Director, Illicit Finance and Anti-Corruption Department, FCDO, Chris Chalmers, said illicit financial flows harmed both countries’ economies and enabled the activities of transnational criminal networks. He said the engagements had helped consolidate cooperation on shared threats and global standards, including public-private partnerships. “The FCDO will continue to partner with Nigeria to operationalise the Joint Financial Intelligence Collaboration,” Chalmers said. Also speaking, Bakari said the increasingly interconnected and transnational nature of illicit financial networks made international cooperation essential. She said Nigeria was strengthening its financial intelligence architecture through initiatives such as JFIC, which would enable public institutions and private-sector partners to work more effective

item.title: Fraud, weak investor protection threaten diaspora investments – NiDCOM
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM) has identified fraudulent investment schemes, unverified investment channels and weak investor protection as major obstacles to attracting investments from Nigerians living abroad. The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of NiDCOM, Abike Dabiri-Erewa, raised the concerns at the opening of the ninth Nigeria Diaspora Investment Summit 2026 in Abuja. She said the challenges had created a trust deficit that must be addressed to encourage more Nigerians in the diaspora to channel their resources into the domestic economy. The summit, organised in collaboration with the Nigeria Diaspora Summit Initiative, has the theme, “Bridging the Trust Gap: Connecting Diaspora Capital with Credible Home-based Opportunities.” Dabiri-Erewa described Nigerians living abroad as a significant economic force, saying their financial resources, expertise and global networks could contribute substantially to Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1tn economy. She, however, noted that concerns about transparency, fraudulent investment schemes and unreliable investment platforms continued to discourage potential investors. The NiDCOM chief called for effective regulatory safeguards, transparent investment processes and credible investment platforms to protect prospective investors and restore confidence. In his keynote address, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria, Shehu Usman Osidi, said the country must move beyond appealing to Nigerians abroad to invest and create an environment where they could independently verify, access and monitor investment opportunities from their locations. Osidi identified fraudulent property transactions, disputed land titles, abandoned projects, unfulfilled contractual obligations and mismanagement of investment funds as some of the factors undermining diaspora investors’ confidence. He called for stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulators and private-sector operators to promote transparency and safeguard diaspora investments. The FMBN chief executive said the Federal Government had taken steps to strengthen engagement with Nigerians abroad through the establishment of NiDCOM and the adoption of the National Diaspora Policy. He said the policy provided a framework for mobilising diaspora resources through investment, trade, entrepreneurship, public-private partnerships and knowledge transfer. Osidi also cited reforms under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly those being pursued through the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council, chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. On efforts to address challenges in the housing sector, he disclosed that the FMBN had introduced the National Housing Fund Diaspora Mortgage Product, which was launched in London on August 7, 2026. item.title: Join BRICS, Nigeria has no business with poverty — Falana tells FG
item.description: …Urges government to prioritise local refining, alternative economic policies By Favour Ulebor, Abuja A Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, has urged the Federal Government to join the BRICS economic bloc and adopt alternative economic policies, declaring that Nigeria has no business with poverty. Falana made the call while delivering the keynote address at the sixth edition of the Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards, organised by Pacesetter Frontier Magazine in Abuja on Tuesday. The human rights lawyer urged the government to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported petroleum products by strengthening domestic refining capacity and pursuing economic policies that promote local production and improve citizens’ welfare. He questioned why Nigeria, despite being a major crude oil-producing country, continued to rely on imported petroleum products to meet domestic consumption needs. Falana also called on the government to explore opportunities offered by BRICS, describing the economic bloc as an organisation established to challenge the dominance of the United States dollar and promote trade among member countries using their respective currencies. He argued that Nigeria needed to reconsider its dependence on economic policies promoted by the Bretton Woods institutions, including the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. He said, “Even within the bourgeois paradigm, within the bourgeois framework, consider some of them, including refining crude oil for domestic consumption in Nigeria. “No country in the world, none, has ever been developed by implementing the policies of these Bretton Woods institutions that were set up to underdevelop the economies of third world countries. “Join, join, join, not be a member country. Join the BRICS. I’m sure you know about the BRICS.” Explaining his position, Falana said the bloc offered opportunities for countries to challenge the dominance of the dollar and strengthen economic cooperation through local currency trade. “It’s an organisation set up to challenge the dominance of the dollar, to challenge the West, to mould the full-fledged members so that we can take advantage and trade among ourselves in your own currencies,” he said. The lawyer also said he had challenged what he described as the abandonment of the Nigeria-China currency swap arrangement. He further raised concerns over revenue losses associated with the suspension of cargo tracking, citing a Nigerian government report produced in 2021. According to him, the report showed that Nigeria lost $32bn during the 13 years in which cargo tracking was suspended, while another $10bn was lost between 2021 and 2025. item.title: Senate summons aviation agencies over flight delays, safety risks
item.description: …Orders probe of prolonged aircraft holding during VIP movements By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has directed its Committee on Aviation to convene an urgent stakeholders’ meeting with relevant aviation authorities over prolonged aircraft holding in the air during Very Important Persons (VIPs) movements and other security-related operations at Nigerian airports. The Senate mandated the committee, chaired by Senator Abdulfatai Buhari (APC, Oyo North), to engage the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) to address the disruptions and recommend measures to prevent their recurrence. The directive followed the adoption of an urgent motion sponsored by Senator Isah Jibrin (APC, Kogi East) during plenary on Tuesday, raising concerns over the safety implications of keeping commercial aircraft airborne for extended periods while awaiting clearance to land. The Senate amended the motion to include the NSIB among the agencies to be engaged and directed the committee to report back within two weeks. Jibrin, who moved the motion under Orders 41 and 51 of the Senate Standing Orders, drew attention to reported instances in which commercial aircraft scheduled to land at Nigerian airports were forced to remain in holding patterns for over an hour because landing operations had been temporarily suspended to accommodate VIP movements. He also noted that some international flights had been diverted to alternative airports within the country when access to their intended destinations was temporarily restricted. While acknowledging the legitimate security considerations surrounding VIP movements, the senator warned that such operations should not compromise aviation safety or unnecessarily disrupt commercial flight schedules. He expressed concern that prolonged airborne holding could increase fuel consumption, deplete operational reserves and expose aircraft to additional risks, including adverse weather conditions, air traffic congestion, diversion challenges and crew duty-time limitations. According to him, commercial aviation depends on coordinated schedules covering departure and arrival slots, fuel planning, crew duty hours, passenger connections, airport operations and air traffic management. He argued that where airport restrictions arising from VIP movements or other security operations were foreseeable, relevant authorities should coordinate ground delays, revised departure slots and flight sequencing rather than allow aircraft to take off and subsequently remain airborne awaiting clearance. The senator further maintained that information about anticipated airport restrictions should guide decisions on departure clearance and the management of arriving aircraft. The Senate expressed concern that prolonged holding could create fuel-related emergencies, particularly where several aircraft were simultaneously awaiting clea

item.title: Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said Monday his office has begun accepting bitcoin for property tax payments, both online and in person, while converting every transaction into dollars before the money reaches the county. Fernandez announced the change in a statement on the Tax Collector’s website, calling it a way to give property owners another option without putting public funds into the asset. Payers can select a cryptocurrency option during online checkout or request it at the counter, then connect a supported exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the payment. A third-party system converts the bitcoin into U.S. dollars at the time of payment, the office said, so it never holds, invests in or manages any cryptocurrency. The office said it still receives the full dollar amount owed and records the transactions in its standard payment reports, without county workers maintaining digital wallets. “Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve,” Fernandez said. “By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust.” He added that the office is “embracing new technology without compromising our responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars.” Whether someone pays with bitcoin or a conventional method, he said, “our office receives the full amount owed in U.S. dollars.” The office did not name the payment processor or say whether bitcoin payments carry a convenience fee. Card and mobile-wallet payments already carry a nonrefundable 2.50% fee online, with a $2.50 minimum, the office’s payment-methods page shows. Traditional options, including checks, cards, cash and fee-free eChecks, remain available. The announcement covers property taxes, and the option is voluntary. JUST IN: Miami-Dade now accepts Bitcoin for property taxes and can be paid both online and in person pic.twitter.com/lI285z4B79 — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 10, 2026 A 4% discount is still on the clock The change landed in the middle of Florida’s property tax collection season. Miami-Dade opened the 2026 tax roll on Oct. 30 and is urging owners to pay by Nov. 30 to lock in a 4% early-payment discount under Florida law . The discount falls to 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with the full amount due in March. Unpaid bills generally become delinquent April 1. Under the office’s existing rules, discounts are based on the date a payment is submitted online or in person. Fernandez has been promoting a “Save the Max” campaign around that calendar, noting that an eligible $5,000 tax bill would save $200 if paid in November. Payments can be made at the office’s 13 locations, through T-Connect mobile units or online around the clock at mdctaxcollector.gov . Miami’s long c

item.title: Trump taps Palantir security chief to run battered US cyber defense agency
item.description: President Donald Trump has nominated Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, putting an executive from the controversial government supplier in line to run America's civilian cyber defense agency. The nomination , announced on Monday, could end CISA's nearly two-year wait for a Senate-confirmed director following Jen Easterly's departure in January 2025. LoSapio has served as Palantir's CISO since September 2024 , having previously led the company's infrastructure and network security team. He first joined the data analytics outfit in 2013, later spent a spell at database company SingleStore, and returned to Palantir in 2017. If confirmed, LoSapio would move from securing Palantir's systems to leading the federal government's main civilian cyber defense agency. CISA protects federal civilian networks and works with critical infrastructure operators, including power, water, and telecommunications providers. It's a substantial job, particularly given the state of the agency he would inherit. CISA has shed more than 1,000 staff, roughly a third of its workforce, since Trump returned to the White House, according to reports . It's now trying to plug the gaps, although acting director Nick Andersen said in September that around 250 would-be recruits were still waiting for security clearance before they could get to work. Andersen has been running CISA since February. With fewer people to go around, CISA is also rethinking where to spend its time. A strategy published last month emphasizes infrastructure whose failure would do the most damage, raising questions about what gets less attention as the agency operates with fewer staff. LoSapio would be the second person Trump has put forward for the role. His previous pick, Sean Plankey, withdrew in April after spending more than a year awaiting confirmation, with his nomination becoming caught up in a dispute involving Republican Senator Rick Scott over Coast Guard contracting. The nomination arrives late in the congressional calendar. If the Senate does not confirm LoSapio before the current Congress ends, Trump would have to nominate him again for consideration by the incoming Democratic-controlled Senate. Palantir, co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, has become a major supplier of technology to US government agencies, including the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Its work with immigration authorities has attracted criticism from civil liberties groups and Democratic lawmakers concerned about surveillance and the handling of sensitive personal information. The controversy isn't confined to the US either. In the UK, WhatsApp messages obtained by campaign group Foxglove this week indicate that Palantir privately lobbied a health minister to consider extending its software into GP patient records, despite that data being expressly excluded from its £330 million NHS England contract for the Federated Data Platform. That revelation follows news

item.title: FG expands health insurance coverage to 24m Nigerians
item.description: …Revitalises 3,526 PHCs, records over 20% drop in maternal deaths …Tinubu administration fulfils 41 health sector commitments — Pate By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has expanded health insurance coverage from 16 million to 24 million Nigerians, revitalised 3,526 primary healthcare centres (PHCs) and recorded a reduction of more than 20 per cent in maternal deaths arising from obstetric emergencies in government-supported facilities over the past three years. The government also said the President Bola Tinubu administration had fulfilled all 41 performance commitments set for the health sector at the beginning of his tenure. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja at the third Nigeria Health Sector-Wide Joint Annual Review (JAR), themed, “Make the Data Count”. Pate attributed the achievements to reforms under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint, which focus on strengthening healthcare governance, improving population health, expanding health financing, promoting local production of medical supplies and enhancing health security. According to him, the progress reflects the collective efforts of federal and state governments, development partners and other stakeholders. He said, “At the beginning of this administration, Mr President set performance commitments for the health sector. I am pleased to report that we have achieved all 41 commitments. These results reflect work across the federation and the institutions represented here today.” The minister disclosed that, for the third consecutive year, all states and more than 8,000 facilities supported by the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) had prepared plans for the coming year, aligned with budget priorities. He said cumulative BHCPF releases since 2019 had reached approximately ₦422.3bn as of October 2026, with ₦323.6bn disbursed to the fund’s gateways, including ₦249.5bn under the Tinubu administration. Pate added that the government had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) to strengthen the tracking of the funds and promote accountability. On health insurance, he said coverage had increased from approximately 16 million to 24 million Nigerians within three years, representing eight million additional enrollees. On primary healthcare delivery, the minister said 3,526 centres had been revitalised in collaboration with state governments and development partners, while work was ongoing on another 900 facilities. He also disclosed that 19,758 skilled birth attendants had been recruited across 22 states, alongside 4,747 community health workers in 10 states, while 78,054 frontline health workers had received training. item.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
item.description: 5 min read NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy. Watch to learn how the presence of a planet modifies the gravitational wave signal from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory could detect a Jupiter-mass planet in such systems up to thousands of light-years away. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Download high-resolution video from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio “The most common source for LISA is expected to be double white dwarf systems, which are binaries composed of white dwarfs in tight orbits,” said Casey McGrath, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. “If an exoplanet also orbits within one of these systems, its presence becomes imprinted on the gravitational wave signal in a way we’ll be able to uncover.” Two papers published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal detail the findings. The first , authored solely by McGrath, examines the detection method and determines the planet masses and orbital periods where it would work best. The second paper , by McGrath and coauthors, investigates how such planets could be confirmed using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope . The possibility of detecting exoplanets around LISA double white dwarf systems was first proposed by Japanese astronomer Naoki Seto in 2008. Led by ESA (European Space Agency), the LISA mission is slated for launch in the mid-2030s. As a collaborative partner, NASA is contributing the telescopes, other critical hardware, and engineering and scientific support as part of its mission to better understand how the universe works. The LISA detection method is similar to one called radial velocity that uses light and is already employed to find exoplanets around nearby stars. As a planet orbits, its gravity tugs on its host star, imparting a small reflex motion, or wobble, onto it. This wobble causes the star’s spectrum to oscillate, with spectral lines shifting from redder wavelengths as the star moves away from us to bluer ones as the star moves toward us. The shift is due to a phenomenon called the Doppler effect . “Something similar occurs with gravitational waves,” said Scott Noble, a theoretical astrophysicist at NASA Goddard and a coauthor on the confirmation paper. “By themselves, double white dwarfs will emit gravitational waves at a nearly continuous frequency. Add a sufficiently massive planet to the system, and its presence causes the binary to experience reflex motion, adding a Doppler modulation to the gravitational signal.” For LISA, this mo

item.title: A robot just built a structure autonomously in space for the 1st time ever
item.description: null A robot just played Tinkertoys in space, assembling the first satellite structure ever made without a human touching the controls. The DARPA-funded project saw a robotic "truss builder" create a reflective antenna using Kapton film, composite fiber tubes and aluminum joints. The implications are huge for future missions, potentially opening up new possibilities to build — or fix — satellites in the final frontier. "This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space ," Sergio Pellegrino, an aerospace and civil engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement on Nov. 5 . The need for such spacecraft will likely rise substantially in the future, as companies assemble giant megaconstellations for cell-phone communications, AI compute and other purposes. Indeed, the ball is already rolling on such ambitious projects, generating enough hype for space startups around the globe to raise a record $20.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 alone. Anything that launches aboard a rocket is limited by the size of that vehicle's fairing — the nose cone that protects payloads during their ride to space. In space, however, the ability to stretch out is practically infinite — after taking into account, of course, engineering and financing constraints. Assembling structures robotically off Earth could therefore be revolutionary, advocates say. And the recent milestone was a step in that direction. "This work could be useful not only for astronomy and astrophysics, but also for communications and other areas, such as building very large solar arrays for space solar power ," said Pellegrino, who's team leader of the truss-building project, a Caltech demonstration mission called Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA). ASTRA built a 1.4-meter-wide (4.5-foot) structure in orbit. That's an impressive achievement, but it just scratches the surface of what DARPA wants to accomplish via a program it calls Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design, or NOM4D for short. "NOM4D's objective is to enable efficient, scalable construction of very large structures in space," NOM4D Program Manager Andrew Detor said in a Nov. 5 DARPA statement . "By 'very large,' I mean hundreds of meters or kilometers in scale. Nothing approaching that scale can be achieved today," Detor added. Concept art for a space-based antenna autonomously assembled by a device that DARPA seeks to develop and operate via its NOM4D program. (Image credit: DARPA/Colie Wertz) ASTRA was a demonstration, allowing researchers to check boxes and identify obstacles before shooting for a bigger goal. And the team did run into issues — specifically, time limitations, which prevented them from building additional sections of the antenna. Still, the researchers were able to prove out the third phase of a larger DARPA project. Pellegrino's team completed the two previous phases — defining the

item.title: Fireworks AI gets burned twice as customer data exposure widens
item.description: Fireworks AI has disclosed another cyberattack in October and a wider customer data exposure involving billing records, datasets, and incomplete model weights. The company, which lets customers train and run AI models, said a third-party cloud provider hosting its research and development machines was compromised on October 23. Attackers used that access the following day to reach Fireworks development systems and run an unauthorized workload. Fireworks suspects links to financially motivated criminals involved in LLMJacking – selling unauthorized access to AI models through illicit gateways. Fireworks grouped the affected data into three categories: Resource metadata: Resource identifiers, display names, descriptions, creation times, and more Billing information: Billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment histories, account balances, and credit usages. Payment card numbers are not saved and therefore unaffected Model weights and datasets: For certain customers, a subset of incomplete model weights and datasets were accessed, Fireworks said Lin Qiao, Fireworks co-founder and CEO, said the apparent motive was not stealing model weights in response to concerns raised by Cantina Security CEO Hari Mulackal. "From what we see attackers are not after weights," said Qiao. "Most downloads were partial and stopped." Render founder and CEO Anurag Goel shared a notification from Notion warning that some chats with its AI assistant may have been exposed through the Fireworks incident. "Following an investigation by the Notion security team, we have determined that your workspace, Render, was among the <1 percent of Notion workspaces that may have been affected by the Fireworks security incident," the email sent to Goel stated. "Some unattributable chat sessions with Notion AI may have been exposed in this incident." Notion said the exposed transcripts lacked separate information linking them to particular users or workspaces. As Reddit users pointed out , however, the conversations themselves could contain identifying details. "Beyond what's in the chat transcript itself, there's no information tying the chat back to your workspace, users, or company," the email added. "No other data from within your workspace is affected." Bloomberg reports that Fireworks is also working with customers including Cursor and Harvey to assess the impact. Fireworks' update confirmed that it worked with Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 team to remediate the attack, which included rotating credentials, isolating affected systems from the network, and tightening up data storage access and monitoring systems. The update did not state how many customers were affected by either of the two attacks in October. Fireworks first disclosed an incident on October 9 after detecting unauthorized use of internal credentials on October 6. item.title: Trump Media (DJT) Pledges 73% of Its Bitcoin to an Options Program as $1 Billion Note Deadline Nears
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Trump Media (DJT) Pledges 73% of Its Bitcoin to an Options Program as $1 Billion Note Deadline Nears Trump Media & Technology Group has pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can reuse the coins, the company disclosed in its third-quarter 10-Q filed Monday, three weeks before holders of its $1 billion in convertible notes can demand cash. The Truth Social parent held approximately 15,649 BTC on Sept. 30, Chief Financial Officer Phillip Juhan said on Monday’s earnings call, along with 7 million shares of BlackRock’s IBIT. Of those coins, 11,385.20 were pledged to what the company calls its bitcoin yield management program. The filing says that program requires Trump Media to post bitcoin as collateral “that the counterparty can rehypothecate at their sole discretion.” The pledged coins carried a fair value of $951.4 million at quarter-end. The 10-Q does not name the counterparty. Another 4,260.73 BTC, worth $356.1 million on Sept. 30, sits as collateral for the convertible notes and cannot be withdrawn or distributed until the indenture’s conditions are met. Together, the two buckets account for about 15,646 BTC, nearly all of the stack Juhan described. How the Trump Media options program works Trump Media sells and buys covered calls and puts on bitcoin, settled in bitcoin, to “generate yield on these assets and increase our principal balance of bitcoin,” the filing says. Premiums arrive in bitcoin and are “immediately rehypothecated to our digital asset manager to reinvest.” At quarter-end it had written calls referencing 4,838.40 BTC at strikes from $68,000 to $92,000 and puts on 1,500 BTC at $75,000 to $80,000, all expiring in October. A risk factor spells out the trade-off. The company says its yield counterparties “may not be rated” by credit agencies, that it is limited in its ability to sell or use deployed bitcoin while the arrangements are open, and that where they are unsecured “we may be unable to recover deployed bitcoin in a counterparty insolvency.” Juhan said Trump Media bought 4,359 bitcoin during the quarter with proceeds from a partial sale of its IBIT position, part of a shift toward “third-party institutional” management of its treasury. A $409.7 million profit and a Nov. 30 deadline The bitcoin rally in the third quarter turned Trump Media profitable on paper. Net income was $409.7 million, driven by a $378.1 million gain on digital assets as bitcoin climbed to about $84,000 on Sept. 30 from about $59,000 on June 30. Adjusted EBITDA was still a loss of $12.3 million, and the company lost $234.2 million over the first nine months. Prices have since moved against the stack. With bitcoin near $74,200 Tuesday morning, the 15,649 coins are worth about $1.16 billion, roughly $145 million less than at quarter-end. The bigger test is the notes. item.title: Amaechi Accuses APC Of Dodging Policy Debate, Focusing On Opposition
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of concentrating on opposition figures rather than presenting its policies and plans to Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State and minister of transportation, said the ruling party was more interested in weakening the opposition than engaging Nigerians on critical national issues. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday. According to him, the APC’s campaign rallies have largely focused on attacking opposition figures, particularly him, rather than addressing issues affecting the country. “The party in power is trying to look for how to weaken the opposition; they are scared. Don’t you see their campaign? Tell me one state they have campaigned in that is not about Amaechi; it’s all Amaechi, Amaechi, Amaechi, Ebonyi, Rivers, Amaechi,” he said. ﻿ Policy Debate Amaechi contrasted the ruling party’s approach with the opposition’s campaign, saying his party had focused on issues such as the economy, social housing and security. “When we were campaigning, we were addressing issues. We addressed the issues of economy, social housing, security,” the ex-minister said. Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. He further argued that the APC was using his name as a recurring subject at its campaign events instead of explaining what it intended to do if re-elected. “You know what I do every morning? I call my children, [and] I say, ‘You see, your father has achieved so much that he is now the issue in the political discourse of Nigeria.’ NDC is not calling my name because we are in opposition. Anywhere APC is going tomorrow, it’s Amaechi they will mention; they won’t mention what they will do,” he said. View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. The former governor also dismissed what he described as the ruling party’s assurances that things would improve in the future, arguing that Nigerians deserved concrete policy proposals rather than promises. “They are not interested; what they are interested in is, ‘don’t worry, things will be better in the future, just put us in power.’ It’s a referendum,” he added. Amaechi contested the ADC presidential primary ahead of the 2027 election but lost to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is currently Atiku’s running mate on the party’s ticket. item.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
item.description: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. DeepMind's physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There's the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that's Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5. DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. item.title: Curiosity Mars rover sizes up new 'Nazca' dig site | Space photo of the day for Nov. 10, 2026
item.description: null NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager, showing the abundance of disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, dubbed "Nazca." (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it. What is it? Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target. MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image. Why is it incredible? Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow. The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

item.title: MARA Sells 13,597 Bitcoin for $1.1 Billion, Says More Sales Are Coming
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine MARA Sells 13,597 Bitcoin for $1.1 Billion, Says More Sales Are Coming MARA Holdings sold 13,597 bitcoin for about $1.1 billion after the third quarter ended and used $750 million of the cash to pay off all of its bitcoin-backed term loans, the miner said Monday in its Q3 shareholder letter. The coins went for roughly $81,039 each. MARA held 34,012 BTC on Sept. 30, so the sale cut about 40% of the stack in a matter of weeks. Repaying the loans returned 17,477 bitcoin that had been pledged as collateral, leaving less than 5% of MARA’s holdings loaned or pledged, the company said. Subtracting the sale from the quarter-end figure implies about 20,400 BTC left, before counting coins mined since. The letter makes clear the selling is not over. “We intend to continue using bitcoin to build cash for purposes such as AI infrastructure opportunities, to satisfy the puts on our convertible notes that become exercisable next year, and potential share repurchases,” MARA wrote. The board also authorized a buyback of up to $500 million of common stock after quarter-end. MARA’s treasury becomes a funding source MARA spent years building one of the largest bitcoin stacks among public companies. The shift away from holding came in stages. The company said it began permitting sales of mined bitcoin in 2025 and in 2026 expanded the policy to cover bitcoin already on its balance sheet. It sold about 26,984 bitcoin for $1.9 billion in the first nine months of the year, including 3,891 BTC in the third quarter at an average of $75,300. It mined 2,247 BTC in the quarter and bought none. Year to date, MARA has cut total debt by $1.4 billion, or 37%. It ended September with $946.5 million in cash and about $3.8 billion in cash and bitcoin combined, plus 1,408 BTC lent out that earned about $2.5 million in interest during the quarter. MARA’s post-quarter sale fetched about $6,800 more per coin than bitcoin’s price near $74,200 on Tuesday morning. Revenue falls as the AI pivot speeds up The quarter’s headline profit came from the coins, not the mines. Revenue fell 35% to $164.2 million from $252.4 million a year earlier, even as energized hashrate rose 18% to 71.2 EH/s. Net income rose to $632.1 million, or $1.28 a diluted share, from $123.1 million, helped by an $885.3 million gain on the fair value of digital assets. Mining itself got slightly more expensive. Purchased energy cost per bitcoin at MARA’s owned sites was $39,674, up from $39,235 a year earlier, while blocks won rose 2% to 644. “Bitcoin built the foundation. Power created the opportunity,” the letter opens, describing a strategy to “maximize the value of every megawatt” MARA controls. MARA said it is targeting two data center leases before year-end but warned that “market conditions are fluid and that timing could slip into next year.” It received FERC approval for its Long Ridge natural gas plant purchase, currently authorized to sell 485 MW, and expects to close in the coming weeks. item.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. Several US media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion. item.title: What is the electrification target at COP31 and can countries meet it?
item.description: Relying on electricity for more of our energy is vital to efforts to limit global warming Christian Hütter/mauritius images GmbH/Alamy One of the key items being discussed at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, this week is a voluntary global target to increase electricity’s share of total final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035. This 35 by 35 target is based on analysis by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) on what is needed to keep the 1.5°C global warming target within reach. Currently, electricity is estimated to make up just 23.4 per cent of the energy delivered to consumers, known as final energy – a figure that has increased by only 6.7 percentage points since 2000. This means that hitting the target will require the rate of electrification to quadruple compared with the first quarter of the 21st century and triple compared with the rate between 2020 and 2025. Judit Hecke at New Climate Institute, a German think tank, says such an acceleration is possible but “the challenge is getting policies, investment and infrastructure moving at the same pace”. Advertisement Progress on renewable energy has been encouraging, with renewables making up a higher proportion of overall electricity production year after year, and renewable capacity additions have been setting new records each year. In 2024, the most recent IRENA data, nearly 32 per cent of global electricity production came from renewable sources compared with just 18 per cent in 2000. Renewable energy capacity has increased from 0.8 terawatts in 2000 to 5.2 terawatts in 2025. But this is a long way from the COP28 pledge for UN member states to reach 11 terawatts of renewable capacity by 2030. However, Hecke points out that the electrification target includes electricity regardless of how it is generated, meaning that a country could make progress while still heavily relying on coal and gas in the power sector. Electrification, renewables and energy efficiency should be looked at together as the “three pillars of the energy transition”, says Hecke. “At COP31, governments should back the target as part of this wider transition and set out how they will deliver it nationally.” Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Jan Rosenow at the University of Oxford says the 35 by 35 target is “broadly the right level of ambition” and it is achievable now that electric vehicles , electrical industrial heat and heat pumps are often the cheapest options. “Most new electricity generation built today is renewables and batteries. And electric technologies are so much more efficient that they cut fossil fuel use even on today’s grids, [which] are getting cleaner every year,” he says. The share of energy supplied by electricity varies widely from sector to sector, with transport a long way behind buildings and industrial applications. item.title: Another contract extension for Fujitsu on the Post Office's Horizon
item.description: The UK Post Office is extending its contract with Fujitsu to give it time to move services to a new supplier, after a scandal that has long marred the relationship between the two. The current contract runs until March 2027, and the publicly owned company has announced a short, time-limited contract extension to cover the transition. Accenture will take over running the Horizon system, which was at the center of a string of miscarriages of justice, from September 2027, after winning a £410 million contract in May this year. Meanwhile, the Post Office is developing a replacement for the aging system to serve its network of 11,500 branches. The Post Office began rolling out the legacy Horizon IT system for accounting in 1999, along with two subsequent upgrades. The electronic point-of-sale (EPOS) and back-end finance system was first implemented by ICL, a UK tech firm majority-owned by Fujitsu in the 1990s and which it fully acquired in 1998 . From 1999 until 2015, around 736 subpostmasters were wrongfully prosecuted and convicted over Horizon errors, devastating lives in the process. The Post Office, Accenture, and Fujitsu have agreed that Fujitsu will hand over the operation of Horizon to Accenture between 1 June and 1 September 2027, with the final date set to be confirmed in March 2027. Accenture is set to "walk in and take over" the current Horizon system by assuming day-to-day operations from Fujitsu, as well as developing the back-end of the new system to replace Horizon. Post Office CEO Neil Brocklehurst said: "Ending our contract with Fujitsu is a critical milestone in Post Office's transformation, and today's agreement secures the transition away from Fujitsu and over to Accenture safely and responsibly to achieve our target of summer 2027. "In addition to ending our contract with Fujitsu, we are also working at pace with our leading technology suppliers, Accenture, OneView Commerce, and Escher, to build a modern, resilient platform able to make everyday life easier for customers and postmasters for years to come." Fujitsu has also been awarded a contract extension to run the UK Government's Emergency Alerts platform until October 2029. The contract is worth £9.6 million ($12.8 million). The company committed to not bid for new public sector contracts while the inquiry into the Horizon scandal continues. ®

item.title: Hyperscale Data (GPUS) Sells Its Last Bitcoin for AI Data Center, Months After Chasing $100 Million Treasury
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Hyperscale Data (GPUS) Sells Its Last Bitcoin for AI Data Center, Months After Chasing $100 Million Treasury Hyperscale Data has sold the last of its bitcoin, the NYSE American-listed company said Tuesday, unloading about 211.56 BTC for roughly $16 million to pay down debt and fund an AI data center in Michigan. The sales were completed by Nov. 8 at about $76,000 per coin. Since it first sold part of its reserve in late July, Hyperscale has sold approximately 1,113 bitcoin for about $74.4 million, the company said. That works out to an average of roughly $66,800 per coin. At today’s price near $74,200, the same 1,113 BTC would be worth about $82.6 million. The company, which trades under the ticker GPUS, said the money will go toward its Michigan site, where it aims to energize the first 10 megawatts of critical IT capacity in December. “We believe bringing that capacity online is our quickest path to profitability,” CEO Will Horne said in the release. “Selling our Bitcoin reserves reduces our exposure to Bitcoin price swings and gives us cash to pay down debt and fund the work in Michigan. We believe that’s the best use of this capital for all our stockholders.” From a $100 million target to zero The exit is a sharp reversal from Hyperscale’s plans this summer. In late July, the company reported holding more than 1,106 bitcoin and said it wanted to build a $100 million digital asset treasury and reach full parity between its bitcoin holdings and its market capitalization. “Every Bitcoin we acquire further strengthens Hyperscale Data’s balance sheet and expands our financial flexibility,” Executive Chairman Milton “Todd” Ault III said at the time. “We intend to continue building our Bitcoin position over time.” A week later, Hyperscale disclosed its first sale , about 150.5 BTC, leaving it with roughly 958.5 BTC as of Aug. 2, even as its Ault Capital Group subsidiary bought about 15 BTC on the open market. The holdings were split between that unit and Sentinum. Ault said then that the company planned to keep a long-term position while tapping it for short-term flexibility, adding, “We are confident in our ability to use Bitcoin as pristine collateral.” Tuesday’s release closes that chapter. Hyperscale said it still mines bitcoin at its Montana site and expects any bitcoin it holds on its balance sheet going forward to come “primarily” from its own mining operations. Hyperscale joins the bitcoin-for-AI trade Hyperscale is the latest public company to give up a bitcoin treasury in favor of data center spending. Keel sold its entire bitcoin treasury for $192 million in the third quarter, and Riot and Hut 8 sold thousands of bitcoin to fund AI buildouts and buybacks. Larger miners are moving the same way. MARA said Monday it sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion after Sept. 30 and plans to keep selling to fund AI infrastructure, convertible note puts and share repurchases. item.title: Onramp Launches Business Bitcoin Accounts With Two-Person Withdrawal Approvals as Wrench Attacks Climb
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Onramp Launches Business Bitcoin Accounts With Two-Person Withdrawal Approvals as Wrench Attacks Climb Onramp launched Onramp Business on Tuesday, a free company account with named users, role-based permissions and two-person withdrawal approvals, as physical attacks on bitcoin holders climbed in the first half of the year. The Austin firm announced the product for companies that want bitcoin on the balance sheet but have balked at leaving it with a single login, a single custodian or a single keyholder. The base account carries a 0.85% trade fee, holds bitcoin at a qualified custodian and is usually verified within a business day. It supports up to three users, including owner, admin and view-only roles, plus an audit trail. Two higher tiers, Onramp Treasury and Onramp Enterprise, launched alongside it. “We spent years watching businesses decide they wanted bitcoin on the balance sheet, then stall the moment their board asked who holds the keys,” said Michael Tanguma, founder and CEO of Onramp. “Nobody had a good answer. Onramp Business gives a company the same controls its bank account already has: named users, approvals on withdrawals, and a record of everything. As the position grows, Onramp Treasury holds it in a vault protected by three independent institutions, so no single party, Onramp included, can lose or move it.” A midyear report recorded 52 physical attacks on bitcoin and crypto holders in the first half of 2026, up 33% from a year earlier. Recorded exposure tied to those incidents rose to about $124 million from $10.5 million. The report notes that a person who can move coins alone can be forced to do so under duress. What the free account does and does not include Onramp Business itself is not Multi-Institution Custody. Bitcoin in the free account sits in cold storage at a qualified custodian, the company’s product page says . Multi-Institution Custody comes with Onramp Treasury, which starts at $375 a month, or $3,600 a year, cuts the trade fee to 0.65% and moves the coins into a vault held in the company’s name. That vault is protected by a 2-of-3 quorum of Onramp, Tetra Trust and CoinCover, so no single institution can lose, move or use the bitcoin. Treasury supports up to five users and two vaults, and includes migration help and continuity planning for leadership changes. A $500 onboarding fee is waived for companies that activate Treasury by Dec. 31. Onramp Enterprise, aimed at funds, miners and large corporate treasuries, is priced by consultation. Onramp has offered Multi-Institution Custody for individuals and institutions since 2023, with a network that also includes BitGo. The firm raised $12.5 million in a Series A in May at a $135 million valuation and has said it holds more than $1 billion in bitcoin under the model, with no security incidents since it was founded. It also launched Onramp Finance in April, combining cash, bitcoin brokerage, IRAs and gold. A crowded treasury trade, and a key-person pr

item.title: FDA warns GLP-1 drugs may pose risk of rare condition that causes vision loss
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration is warning that popular obesity drugs—including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro—may carry a "potential increased risk" of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss. In a drug safety communication Monday , the FDA said it will now require makers of GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs to add a warning about that risk on their drug labels. The specific eye condition it warns of is called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy or NAION . The condition is caused by restricted blood flow to the optic nerve, which leads to swelling and cell death and ultimately damages the nerve, causing abrupt vision loss that can often be permanent. It's unknown how GLP-1 drugs may cause NAION. The condition is rare overall, occurring in somewhere between two and 10 people in 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmologists. These small numbers have made it more difficult to determine with certainty if there is a connection. Further complicating the potential link is the fact that the risk factors for developing NAION are common among patients taking GLP-1 drugs. The risk factors include diabetes, cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea. Read full article Comments

Bitcoin Price Trades Down Near $73,500 After Hot CPI Print Lifts Fed Hike Bets
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Down Near $73,500 After Hot CPI Print Lifts Fed Hike Bets Bitcoin price traded near $73,500 on Tuesday morning, down about 1% over the past day and roughly $32,000 below its price one year ago, after a hotter-than-expected inflation report revived fears of a larger Federal Reserve rate hike, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The U.S. consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, climbed 0.3% against forecasts for 0.2%. Bitcoin price had been holding near $74,300 in the minutes before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. It dropped to about $73,400 right after the print, briefly undercutting Monday’s overnight low of $73,477 , before steadying in the high-$73,000s. JUST IN: U.S. CPI inflation comes in at 0.4% MoM, higher than expectations Bitcoin falls below $74,000 on the news. pic.twitter.com/Zxq3LtVwAd — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 10, 2026 Food prices jumped 0.5% on the month, energy rose 0.7% and gasoline gained 1.0%. Housing costs increased 0.3%. The report will not carry an annual inflation rate. The government shutdown in October 2025 kept the Bureau of Labor Statistics from collecting a full set of prices, so there is no comparable figure. Bank of America estimated before the release that the annual rates were running near 3.8% for headline and 2.7% for core. Fed hike bets build around the bitcoin price Bond traders moved first. Two- to five-year Treasury yields rose at least 10 basis points on the day after the print, and traders boosted bets on a half-point hike when the Fed meets on Dec. 9. That was the scenario Fed Governor Christopher Waller laid out hours earlier. He said he is “leaning toward” a December increase and would back “more robust action” if inflation ran hotter than expected. “In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Before the data, markets had already largely priced in a quarter-point move. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no yield, and that math has capped the bitcoin price since Friday’s strong jobs report. Bitcoin had already been soft overnight. It lost about 1.4% from midnight UTC before the data, even as Asian markets rallied. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 4.39% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 2.87%, while oil kept falling after President Donald Trump called fresh strikes on Iran “highly unlikely.” Stock futures were mixed going into the release. Dow futures rose 156 points, or 0.3%, while Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.4% after Monday’s rally gave the S&P 500 its best day since April 8. Commodities slipped too. West Texas Intermediate crude traded near $84 a barrel, its lowest since late August, and gold fell just over 1% to below $4,100 an ounce. ETF outflows leave the bitcoin price exposed Fun

item.title: Polestar has a new look with its Formula 2030 concept
item.description: Perhaps only a small percentage of Ars readers will care about the Polestar 2030 concept, debuted today by the electric automaker. Spun out of Volvo—once upon a time, Polestar was a racing team—the brand has leveraged the resources of parent-automaker Geely to create electric vehicles that marry a modern minimalist style with rewarding driving dynamics . But you now can’t buy any Polestars in the US , since Geely is Chinese, and banning Chinese-owned car brands enjoys remarkable bipartisan support in Congress. The Formula 2030 is about the same length as a Polestar 2 but with a very low roofline. If anything, the two-box shape reminds me of the Saab Aero-X, one of the final concepts from the then-terminal Swedish automaker. (In many ways, Polestar has adopted Saab’s mantle.) Credit: Polestar These rear lights will show up in production Polestars. In 2008, Saab showed off the Aero-X concept. Credit: Scott Barbour/Getty Images Polestar says the concept fits into its own segment somewhere between the next Polestar 2 and the Polestar 7—it numbers its cars chronologically (mostly), not based on size—although it’s not saying if the hatchback form factor will go into series production. Successfully packaging the rear seat passengers and a lithium-ion battery pack is something a concept needn’t worry about, after all. Rather, it’s a styling exercise, or more than one.
